# APPENDIX 1 — TIER 0 TOKEN QUICK REFERENCE

## A1.0 — `MotionTokens` IS VERIFIED (complete, exact API)

Every member below was read directly from `lib/theme/motion_tokens.dart`. **Use these exact
names — do not substitute, and do not inline a literal `Duration` or `Curve` where one of
these applies.** The extension static is named `ReducedMotion`, not `MotionTokens`; prefer the
class API `MotionTokens.accessibleDuration(context, duration)` in new code.

```dart
abstract class MotionTokens {
  // ── DURATIONS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static const instantFeedback  = Duration(milliseconds: 90);
  static const microInteraction = Duration(milliseconds: 120);
  static const fast             = microInteraction;          // alias
  static const control          = Duration(milliseconds: 180);
  static const standard         = Duration(milliseconds: 220);
  static const emphasized       = Duration(milliseconds: 350);
  static const spatial          = Duration(milliseconds: 450);
  static const ambient          = Duration(milliseconds: 900);
  static const celebration      = Duration(milliseconds: 1200);

  // ── CURVES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static const enter         = Curves.easeOutCubic;   // things ARRIVING
  static const exit          = Curves.easeInCubic;    // things LEAVING
  static const spring        = Curves.easeOutBack;    // overshoot / playful
  static const symmetric     = Curves.easeInOutCubic; // both ends
  static const standardCurve = symmetric;             // alias
  static const decelerate    = Curves.decelerate;     // fast-start ease-out

  // ── STAGGER ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static const staggerStep = Duration(milliseconds: 40);
  static const staggerMax  = Duration(milliseconds: 300);
  static Duration staggerDelay(int index, {int cap = 8});

  // ── ACCESSIBILITY ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  static Duration accessibleDuration(BuildContext context, Duration normal);
}

/// Existing compatibility extension in lib/theme/motion_tokens.dart.
extension ReducedMotion on MotionTokens {
  static Duration respectReducedMotion(BuildContext context, Duration normal);
}
```

**Consequences you must respect:**

1. **`staggerDelay` takes an `int` index**, not a `Duration`: `MotionTokens.staggerDelay(3)`
   → 120ms. It is capped at `staggerMax` (300ms) after index 8. So
   `staggerDelay(6)` = **240ms**, which is what TASK-008's choreography maths assumes.
2. **`enter` vs `decelerate`.** Both are ease-out, but they are *different curves*.
   `MotionTokens.enter` (= `Curves.easeOutCubic`) is the correct token for an **entering**
   element — it is semantically named for that purpose. `MotionTokens.decelerate`
   (= `Curves.decelerate`) starts faster and is more aggressive; use it only for a deliberate
   fast-settle. **Entrance animations use `MotionTokens.enter`.**
3. **`enter` / `exit` are the exact curves** already written by hand in `main.dart`'s tab
   transition (`Curves.easeOutCubic` / `Curves.easeInCubic`) — so TASK-007's replacement is a
   pure token substitution with **byte-identical rendering**.
4. **Reduced-motion APIs:** `MotionTokens.accessibleDuration(context, normal)` is a static
   method on `MotionTokens`. `respectReducedMotion(context, normal)` belongs to the
   `ReducedMotion` extension and is called as `ReducedMotion.respectReducedMotion(...)`, not
   `MotionTokens.respectReducedMotion(...)`. Prefer `MotionTokens.accessibleDuration` in new
   code. Do not call either API from `initState` if it depends on `MediaQuery`; defer the
   inherited lookup to `didChangeDependencies` or a valid build-time path.

**`AzRadius`, `AzSpace`, `AzText`, `AzElevation` and `AzMoney` are created by this document**
(TASK-001 / TASK-002 / TASK-009a), so their member names are authoritative here. Verify with
`rg -n "static" lib/theme/az_radius.dart` if in doubt.

# APPENDIX 3 — GLOSSARY

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Token** | A named design constant (a radius, a duration, a colour role). Never a literal. |
| **Bridge getter** | A getter on `AzamanColors` that maps a Material 3 `ColorScheme` role onto an existing Azaman role, so the framework can never introduce a colour we did not choose. |
| **Leakage** | A framework widget rendering in Flutter's baseline M3 palette instead of Azaman's, because a role was left unset. |
| **Directional light** | The app's single implied light source at the top-left. Drives rim highlight (top/left), rim shade (bottom/right), and downward shadow offsets. |
| **Specular streak** | The soft top-left highlight on a glass surface that makes it read as light-bending rather than flat. |
| **Swap point** | `_kTabSwapPoint` (0.4) — the fraction of the tab-transition controller at which the painted page changes. Must be ≥ the point where outgoing opacity reaches 0. |
| **Fast-out / slow-in** | The rule that an exiting element uses an ease-IN curve (leaves quickly) and an entering element uses an ease-OUT curve (arrives slowly). Violating it makes motion feel undirected. |
| **Surgical** | A change that can be applied or reverted in isolation, leaves the build green, and touches only explicitly listed files. |
| **Const presets** | `AzRadius.brMd` etc. — needed because `BorderRadius.circular(x)` is not a `const` constructor, but `BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(x))` is. |

# PART F — IMPLEMENTATION READINESS, MISSING OWNERS & SPEC ERRATA

**Date:** 2026-09-25  
**Authority:** This part supersedes older blanket `SPEC READY` claims and the old PART E
coverage claim. It is based on the supplied assessment, full audit, sub-agent review, and a
targeted read of the supplied Flutter archive. The archive is 963 entries; its platform files,
lockfile, money flows, hubs/chat surfaces, theme/motion implementation, and relevant existing
primitives were checked. No app source was changed in this review.

## F.1 Executive verdict

The brief is a strong design direction and already contains valuable concrete work: token
scales, money formatting, a reduced-motion concept, marketplace behavior, and thoughtful
component-specific tests. It is **not yet safe to execute as written**. Several early tasks
contain deterministic compile errors, replacement anchors/fences do not match, and some
verification probes contradict the code they introduce. Fix the prerequisite specs before
letting implementation proceed; do not infer readiness from the existence of a long code block.

The largest missing product-quality loops are:

1. **Money movement trust:** send, deposit, and withdrawal currently have different review,
   confirmation, pending, success, and failure semantics. This is higher priority than adding
   another decorative hero effect.
2. **Messaging consistency:** there are two conversation hubs and the trade chat has distinct
   bubble/composer implementations.
3. **Accessibility of existing UI:** newly authored widgets having Semantics is not a remediation
   pass for current icon-only controls, target sizes, contrast, scaling, and motion.
4. **Performance/resource lifetime:** Offstage tabs keep state mounted; perpetual tickers,
   polling, and renderer ownership need explicit lifecycle rules.
5. **Trustworthy data and theme parity:** demo/fake metrics must never read as live financial or
   business data; the storefront theme and backdrop remain separate sources of visual truth.

Premium retention should come from useful financial clarity, reliable follow-through, and
memorable but restrained interactions—not streak pressure, artificial scarcity, or motion that
tries to keep users compulsively engaged.

## F.4 Recommended order and dependency control

1. **Gate the toolchain and repair Tier 0 specs:** TASK-001, then corrected TASK-002 and TASK-003, then TASK-004/005/006. Run the supported Android build. Do not start dependent specs while any prerequisite is `BLOCKED`.
2. **Ship the first-use shell and balance experience:** corrected TASK-007/008/009a–009d/010; prioritize truthful balances and refresh states above additional always-on effects. TASK-010b follows corrected TASK-010 and a reviewed TASK-011 contract.
3. **Close the core money loop early:** NEW-P and NEW-R should be promoted ahead of Tier 3 spectacle work. Run send/deposit/withdraw as separate end-to-end journeys with loading, cancel, pending, success, failure, and retry coverage.
4. **Proceed vertical by vertical:** TASK-011 through TASK-015 only after each spec is re-reviewed. Do not assume a blueprint enum or transition is implemented because the model declares it.
5. **Consolidate durable foundations:** NEW-Q/NEW-S/NEW-T/NEW-U, then escrow/Susu/artifacts/sound. Keep NEW-V on a product/backend track.

## F.5 Acceptance rules for every future “premium” task

- One primary user goal per screen; one hero treatment at most. Ambient motion must be informative, rare, visibility-aware, and disabled/reduced when requested.
- Every money action must name the source of truth, distinguish accepted from settled, prevent accidental duplicate submits, retain an error/retry path, and never show fabricated success.
- New state/UI must cover loading, empty, partial, offline, failure, and completed states when the underlying flow can reach them; explicit “not available” is better than fake live data.
- Tests must verify user-visible state contracts and gestures, not raw implementation symbol counts. Exclude prose comments from zero-match probes; probe semantics or production use sites.
- Keep motion/contrast/tap-target checks alongside visual review. Run `flutter test`, `flutter analyze`, and the A.5 supported-target build before marking a task done.
- No new package, API rename, backend payload change, or broad repo rewrite is implied by these additions. Propose and approve those separately.

## F.6 — NEW-P: money movement review, commit, and honest result

**Status:** implementation spec added here; must pass this task's probes and supported-target build.  
**Scope:** `SendMoneyScreen`, `WithdrawalScreen`, and the already-existing deposit flow only. No backend,
router, provider, or request-schema change. The purpose is to share a review/result grammar while
keeping each payment rail's security and settlement rules intact.

### Why this is additive to existing work

The archive already has valuable rail-specific protections: saved-recipient lookup and the
`/finance/internal-transfer` request, a Moolre deposit with optional account-name validation / OTP /
reference-matched socket confirmation, and withdrawal's fee calculation / whitelist / biometric
`SlideToConfirm`. Keep those. The gap is the user-visible **review and outcome contract**: send has
no review and an inline success string; withdrawal currently shows a snackbar then pops; deposit
already distinguishes prompt-sent from socket-confirmed but auto-confirms after a timer in demo mode.
This spec does not replace the rails with a new generic form.

### Financial truth contract

| Rail | UI state on 2xx | UI state on authoritative settlement | Never show |
|---|---|---|---|
| Internal transfer | `accepted` unless the response contract explicitly proves ledger completion | `confirmed` only if the documented response says final transfer committed | fabricated reference, recipient balance, or “cleared” language |
| Mobile-money deposit | `pending` (“Prompt sent; approve on your phone”) | `confirmed` only on the existing matching `onDepositSuccess` reference | `confirmed` from OTP acceptance or a timer |
| Mobile-money / crypto withdrawal | `accepted` / `pending` according to the endpoint response | `confirmed` only if an authoritative status is returned or later read | “Paid”/“landed” from request acceptance |

In demo mode, label the action `Demo` and the outcome `Simulated — no funds moved`; never claim
that a real transfer, deposit, or withdrawal settled.

- `lib/widgets/finance_action_result_panel.dart`
- `lib/providers/finance_action_provider.dart`
- `test/widgets/finance_action_result_panel_test.dart`
- `test/screens/send_money_review_test.dart`

### Files — MODIFY

- `lib/screens/send_money_screen.dart`
- `lib/screens/withdrawal_screen.dart`
- `lib/screens/deposit_screen.dart`
- `test/` additions listed above only; do not touch backend/services/router contracts.

### Step P.1 — Add a typed result view model and result panel

Create `lib/widgets/finance_action_result_panel.dart`:

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';
import 'package:hugeicons_pro/hugeicons.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/az_space.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/az_text.dart';

/// A UI outcome, not a backend transaction state. `accepted` means the request
/// endpoint accepted the request; only `confirmed` means the rail verified it.
enum FinanceActionStatus { accepted, pending, confirmed, failed, simulated }

class FinanceActionResultPanel extends ConsumerWidget {
  final FinanceActionStatus status;
  final String title;
  final String message;
  final String? reference;
  final String? primaryLabel;
  final VoidCallback? onPrimary;
  final String? secondaryLabel;
  final VoidCallback? onSecondary;

  const FinanceActionResultPanel({
    super.key,
    required this.status,
    required this.title,
    required this.message,
    this.reference,
    this.primaryLabel,
    this.onPrimary,
    this.secondaryLabel,
    this.onSecondary,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    final colors = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((theme) => theme.colors));
    final (tone, icon) = switch (status) {
      FinanceActionStatus.accepted =>
        (colors.accent, HugeIconsSolid.checkmarkCircle01),
      FinanceActionStatus.pending =>
        (colors.warning, HugeIconsSolid.clock01),
      FinanceActionStatus.confirmed =>
        (colors.success, HugeIconsSolid.checkmarkCircle01),
      FinanceActionStatus.failed =>
        (colors.danger, HugeIconsSolid.alertCircle),
      FinanceActionStatus.simulated =>
        (colors.textTertiary, HugeIconsSolid.informationCircle),
    };

    return Semantics(
      liveRegion: true,
      label: '$title. $message',
      child: Container(
        width: double.infinity,
        padding: AzSpace.cardInset,
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: colors.card,
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(20),
          border: Border.all(color: tone.withValues(alpha: 0.28)),
        ),
        child: Column(
          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
          children: [
            Center(
              child: Container(
                width: 56,
                height: 56,
                alignment: Alignment.center,
                decoration: BoxDecoration(
                  shape: BoxShape.circle,
                  color: tone.withValues(alpha: 0.12),
                ),
                child: Icon(icon, color: tone, size: 28),
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: AzSpace.md),
            Text(title, textAlign: TextAlign.center,
                style: AzText.titleXl.copyWith(color: colors.textPrimary)),
            const SizedBox(height: AzSpace.xs),
            Text(message, textAlign: TextAlign.center,
                style: AzText.body.copyWith(color: colors.textSecondary)),
            if (reference != null && reference!.isNotEmpty) ...[
              const SizedBox(height: AzSpace.md),
              SelectableText(
                'Reference: $reference',
                textAlign: TextAlign.center,
                style: AzText.bodyS.copyWith(color: colors.textTertiary),
              ),
            ],
            if (primaryLabel != null && onPrimary != null) ...[
              const SizedBox(height: AzSpace.lg),
              SizedBox(
                height: 52,
                child: FilledButton(
                  onPressed: onPrimary,
                  child: Text(primaryLabel!, style: AzText.button),
                ),
              ),
            ],
            if (secondaryLabel != null && onSecondary != null)
              TextButton(onPressed: onSecondary, child: Text(secondaryLabel!)),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

`FinanceActionStatus.accepted` and `pending` are visually distinct and must not share
confirmation haptics or copy. A result reference is optional and must come from the response;
never generate a fake transaction ID.

### Step P.2 — Add one injectable internal-transfer submission seam

Create `lib/providers/finance_action_provider.dart`:

```dart
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import 'package:azaman/services/api_client.dart';

typedef InternalTransferSubmitter =
    Future<http.Response> Function(Map<String, dynamic> payload);

/// Test seam for the existing transfer endpoint. Production preserves ApiClient's
/// auth, timeout, demo interceptor, and response semantics.
final internalTransferSubmitterProvider = Provider<InternalTransferSubmitter>((ref) {
  final api = ref.watch(apiClientProvider);
  return (payload) => api.post('/finance/internal-transfer', payload);
});
```

This is an additive UI/test seam: do not change `ApiClient`, endpoint, authentication,
request keys, or response parsing. Tests override this provider with an in-memory fake.

### Step P.3 — Add an explicit transfer review before the existing request

In `lib/screens/send_money_screen.dart`:

1. Import `package:azaman/config.dart`, `package:azaman/utils/az_money.dart`,
   `package:azaman/providers/finance_action_provider.dart`,
   `package:azaman/widgets/finance_action_result_panel.dart`, and
   `package:azaman/widgets/azaman_confirm_sheet.dart`. Keep the existing public
   `const SendMoneyScreen({super.key})` constructor unchanged. Retain `motion_tokens.dart` only if
   the final result transition actually uses a token.
2. Add private state fields for the accepted result (`FinanceActionStatus?`, summary message,
   optional response reference, and a snapshot of recipient/amount/note for the receipt view).
3. Keep validation before review. Validate finite amount `> 0`, recipient identifier presence,
   and available balance without mutating the UI to a submitted state.
4. Replace `_send()` with this ordered flow:
   - Guard `_isLoading` and `_recipient == null` first.
   - Parse the amount, reject null/non-finite/`<=0`, and reject an amount above current
     `availableBalance` with a field-level error.
   - Snapshot the destination display name, AZM ID, amount, and optional note before awaiting.
   - Call `AzamanConfirmSheet.show` with title `Review transfer`, a message that lists
     recipient name + AZM ID, exact `AzMoney.usdc(amount)`, and optional note, confirm label
     `Send USDC`, and `destructive: false`. If the user cancels/dismisses or the State unmounts,
     return without a request.
   - Set `_isLoading = true` only after confirmation. Read
     `internalTransferSubmitterProvider` and submit exactly the existing payload:
     `recipientIdentifier`, `amountUsdc`, optional `note`.
   - Treat 200/201 as **accepted** unless the endpoint's documented response contract explicitly
     contains a final-ledger confirmation. Parse a response reference only if it exists; do not
     infer settlement from HTTP success alone. Store the snapshotted request summary, clear the
     editable recipient/amount/note only after accepted, and show `FinanceActionResultPanel` with
     “Transfer request received” / “Your request was accepted. Check Activity for status.”
   - On `ApiException`, connection error, or non-2xx response, retain safe form input, show the
     existing inline error, and leave Send enabled for retry. Do not pop the route.
   - Set `_isLoading = false` in a mounted-safe `finally` block. Prevent a duplicate request
     while the confirmation or request is active.
5. Render the accepted result as the primary body state until the user selects `Done` or
   `Send another`; the action clears only local review/result state and returns to the form.
   The panel's copy must say `accepted`/`received`, not `settled`/`cleared` unless the backend
   contract proves that exact state. If `AppConfig.demoMode` and the configured demo interceptor
   returns a success response, use `FinanceActionStatus.simulated` and the persistent copy
   `Demo mode — no funds were moved`; never label that response accepted or confirmed.
6. Replace the forced line `$${...}` on contacts/history surfaces only where the existing model
   identifies currency as USDC. Do not infer currency from sign alone.

#### P.3a — Exact `_send()` replacement

Add these private fields beside the current `_recipient`, `_error`, and `_successMessage` fields:

```dart
  bool _isReviewing = false;
  FinanceActionStatus? _transferResultStatus;
  String? _transferResultTitle;
  String? _transferResultMessage;
  String? _transferResultReference;
  String? _transferResultRecipient;
  double? _transferResultAmount;
```

In `_send()`, keep the existing endpoint and payload keys; replace the method body with:

```dart
  Future<void> _send() async {
    if (_isLoading || _isReviewing || _recipient == null) return;
    final amount = double.tryParse(_amountController.text.trim());
    if (amount == null || !amount.isFinite || amount <= 0) {
      setState(() => _error = 'Enter a valid amount.');
      return;
    }
    final available = ref.read(authProvider).user?.availableBalance ?? 0.0;
    if (amount > available) {
      setState(() => _error = 'Amount exceeds your available USDC balance.');
      return;
    }

    final recipient = Map<String, dynamic>.from(_recipient!);
    final identifier = recipient['azamanId']?.toString().isNotEmpty == true
        ? recipient['azamanId']
        : recipient['username'];
    if (identifier == null || identifier.toString().trim().isEmpty) {
      setState(() => _error = 'Choose a valid recipient before continuing.');
      return;
    }
    final note = _noteController.text.trim();
    final recipientLabel = (recipient['fullName'] ?? recipient['username'] ??
            recipient['azamanId'] ?? 'Recipient')
        .toString();

    setState(() {
      _isReviewing = true;
      _error = null;
    });
    final confirmed = await AzamanConfirmSheet.show(
      context,
      title: 'Review transfer',
      message: 'Send ${AzMoney.usdc(amount)} to $recipientLabel'
          '${recipient['azamanId'] == null ? '' : ' · ${recipient['azamanId']}'}'
          '${note.isEmpty ? '' : '\nNote: $note'}',
      confirmLabel: 'Send USDC',
      destructive: false,
    );
    if (!mounted) return;
    setState(() => _isReviewing = false);
    if (confirmed != true) return;

    setState(() {
      _isLoading = true;
      _error = null;
    });
    // AzamanConfirmSheet already emits the commit haptic when the user confirms;
    // do not emit a second commit at request start or pretend funds have landed.
    try {
      final submit = ref.read(internalTransferSubmitterProvider);
      final response = await submit({
        'recipientIdentifier': identifier,
        'amountUsdc': amount,
        if (note.isNotEmpty) 'note': note,
      });
      if (!mounted) return;

      final simulated = AppConfig.demoMode;
      setState(() {
        _transferResultStatus = simulated
            ? FinanceActionStatus.simulated
            : FinanceActionStatus.accepted;
        _transferResultTitle = simulated ? 'Demo transfer' : 'Transfer request received';
        _transferResultMessage = simulated
            ? 'Demo mode — no funds were moved.'
            : 'Your transfer request was accepted. Check Activity for its current status.';
        // The endpoint response reference is intentionally not guessed. Add it
        // only after its exact response contract is verified from backend docs.
        _transferResultReference = null;
        _transferResultRecipient = recipientLabel;
        _transferResultAmount = amount;
        _recipient = null;
      });
      if (!simulated) AzamanHaptics.commit();
      _amountController.clear();
      _noteController.clear();
    } catch (error) {
      if (mounted) {
        setState(() => _error = error is ApiException
            ? error.message
            : 'Transfer failed. Check your connection and retry.');
      }
      AzamanHaptics.error();
    } finally {
      if (mounted) setState(() => _isLoading = false);
    }
  }
```

**Imports for this exact method:** `package:azaman/config.dart`,
`package:azaman/providers/finance_action_provider.dart`, `package:azaman/utils/az_money.dart`,
and `package:azaman/widgets/azaman_confirm_sheet.dart`, plus the existing `api_client.dart`
import (for `ApiException`). Do not create a second `ApiClient` here; the injected provider is the
test seam and still delegates to the canonical `apiClientProvider`.

At the top of `build`, if `_transferResultStatus != null`, render `FinanceActionResultPanel` in a
`Center`/`ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: 420)` within the existing `Scaffold` body, passing the saved
result fields and a `Done` callback that clears only the result snapshot. This is an in-place
result; do not pop the route. Disable the primary action while `_isReviewing || _isLoading`.
Use `_transferResultRecipient` and `_transferResultAmount` for an optional summary row such as
`Sent to <name> · GH₵` only when a verified current quote exists; the request itself remains USDC.
Do not display a GHS estimate when rate is unavailable.

1. **Bottom navigation:** wrap each `_NavButton` with a single labelled `Semantics(button: true,
   selected: isSelected, label: item.label)`; include unread count / active-trade / order badge in
   `value` (e.g. `3 unread`) rather than exposing the badge as a separate unlabeled icon. Give the
   tappable region a minimum 48×48 logical-pixel box without changing the 62px outer pill or
   `PremiumBottomNav` public constructor. Hide duplicate child icon/label semantics using

2. **Home eye control:** raise the current 40×40 target to at least 48×48; provide a dynamic

3. **Notification bell:** raise its hit target to ≥48×48; label the action and unread count (pluralize

4. **Action pills and horizontal rails:** expose a meaningful horizontal-scroll hint and retain
   focus order left-to-right. Each control needs a labelled semantic button whose label matches
   the visible destination. Do not hide the only action label when the nav compresses; compression

5. **Recent activity/live quote:** expose each row as a grouped semantic item: transaction name,
   signed amount + currency, status (`Pending`, `Failed`, or `Cancelled` when applicable), and
   date. For a rate, announce pair, rate, source/freshness if present, and unavailable/stale state;

6. **Chat/send/story controls:** label send, attachment, microphone, clear-reply, story previous/next,
   pause, reply, and reaction controls. Raise any currently sub-48dp interactive target to 48dp
   using hit-test padding, not by enlarging the visible glyph. Swipe-only actions need an equivalent
   labelled action/menu reachable by touch/keyboard.
7. **Text/contrast/motion:** financial values must remain readable at platform text scale 2.0 with
   no clipped digits; normal text contrast ≥4.5:1 and large text ≥3:1; every new/changed nonessential
   animation reads `MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf(context)` or the corrected `MotionTokens` API.
   Keep meaningful state changes (pending/confirmed/error) available without animation.

## G.1 — TASK-026: Sensory & motion preference plumbing

**Status on completion:** mark `DONE` only after Step 6's full probe set and the A.5 build pass.

### Why (verified gap — new finding F-062)

The premium layer Part G adds is only *premium* if the user can switch it off. Today they cannot:

- `lib/providers/settings_provider.dart` exposes exactly four booleans — `push_notifications`,
  `trade_alerts`, `chat_notifications`, `vendor_tag_enabled` (L21-31, L46-49) — plus currency,
  language and HQ shortcuts. **There is no haptics flag, no sound flag and no motion flag.**
  Probe: `rg -n "haptic|sound" lib/providers/settings_provider.dart` → no hits.
- `lib/utils/azaman_haptics.dart` L23-27 promises in its own header: *"One place to globally turn it
  off if a user disables haptics in Settings (the existing `settingsProvider.haptics` flag —
  wire-in follow-up in Phase H2)."* **That flag does not exist.** The stated contract is unfulfilled.
- 246 raw `HapticFeedback.*` calls plus 63 importers of `AzamanHaptics` mean a user who wants no
  haptics has no path to that outcome. On Android that is an accessibility expectation, not a nicety.

So `TASK-006` (one vocabulary) and `TASK-020` (sound) are both *incomplete* until a preference
exists. TASK-026 is that preference; it also supplies the single resolver that answers "does this
screen reduce motion right now?", which `TASK-024` then consumes.

- `lib/providers/sensory_provider.dart`
- `lib/widgets/sensory_preferences_section.dart`
- `test/sensory_provider_test.dart`

### Step 1 — NEW `lib/providers/sensory_provider.dart`

```dart
// lib/providers/sensory_provider.dart
// =============================================================================
// SENSORY & MOTION PREFERENCES  (TASK-026)
//
// The user's right to turn the premium layer OFF.
//
// Why a dedicated provider instead of new fields on SettingsProvider?
//   * `settings_provider.dart` is load-bearing (Appendix 2) and is read on nearly
//     every frame by 30+ screens. Adding fields to it widens that blast radius for
//     no gain.
//   * The consumers of this gate are STATIC helpers (`AzamanHaptics`, `AzSound`)
//     that have no BuildContext. `AzSensory` below is the single static sink they
//     read, and it is written from exactly one place — this notifier.
//
// Defaults are deliberately conservative:
//   haptics          ON   — matches today's behaviour (246 raw calls already fire)
//   sound            ON, but SUCCESS-ONLY (tick / whoosh stay opt-in extras)
//   ambient motion   ON   — exactly one ambient loop is allowed, on Home only
//   reduce motion    null — null means "follow the OS"; true/false are explicit
//                           user overrides. null is NOT the same as false.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

class SensoryPreferences {
  final bool hapticsEnabled;
  final bool soundEnabled;

  /// When true, only success / coin / rip play. The UI tick and the transition
  /// whoosh stay silent. Default = true, because a tick on every tap is the
  /// fastest way to make an app's sound feel cheap.
  final bool soundSuccessOnly;

  /// Home's (and only Home's) ambient loop: the Level-5 sheen drift.
  /// Off means the app is completely still when untouched.
  final bool ambientMotionEnabled;

  /// null → follow the OS (`MediaQuery.disableAnimations`).
  final bool? forceReduceMotion;

  const SensoryPreferences({
    this.hapticsEnabled = true,
    this.soundEnabled = true,
    this.soundSuccessOnly = true,
    this.ambientMotionEnabled = true,
    this.forceReduceMotion,
  });

  /// The single answer to "should this screen reduce motion right now?".
  bool reducesMotion({required bool osDisableAnimations}) =>
      forceReduceMotion ?? osDisableAnimations;
}

/// Static sink read by context-free helpers. Written only by [SensoryProvider].
class AzSensory {
  const AzSensory._();

  static bool hapticsEnabled = true;
  static bool soundEnabled = true;
  static bool soundSuccessOnly = true;
  static bool ambientEnabled = true;
  static bool reduceMotionOverrideIsSet = false;
  static bool reduceMotionOverride = false;

  /// Idempotent, and safe to call before the provider has loaded (defaults apply).
  static void apply(SensoryPreferences p) {
    hapticsEnabled = p.hapticsEnabled;
    soundEnabled = p.soundEnabled;
    soundSuccessOnly = p.soundSuccessOnly;
    ambientEnabled = p.ambientMotionEnabled;
    final forced = p.forceReduceMotion;
    reduceMotionOverrideIsSet = forced != null;
    reduceMotionOverride = forced ?? false;
  }
}

class SensoryProvider extends ChangeNotifier {
  SensoryPreferences _prefs = const SensoryPreferences();
  bool _isLoaded = false;

  SensoryPreferences get prefs => _prefs;
  bool get isLoaded => _isLoaded;

  /// Preference keys. Prefixed `az_` so they can never collide with the
  /// `push_notifications` / `trade_alerts` family owned by SettingsProvider.
  static const kHaptics = 'az_haptics_enabled';
  static const kSound = 'az_sound_enabled';
  static const kSoundSuccessOnly = 'az_sound_success_only';
  static const kAmbient = 'az_ambient_motion_enabled';

  /// Sentinel storage for a tri-state boolean: -1 unset, 0 forced-off, 1 forced-on.
  static const kReduceOverride = 'az_reduce_motion_override';

  SensoryProvider() {
    _load();
  }

  Future<void> _load() async {
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    final reduceRaw = prefs.getInt(kReduceOverride) ?? -1;
    _prefs = SensoryPreferences(
      hapticsEnabled: prefs.getBool(kHaptics) ?? true,
      soundEnabled: prefs.getBool(kSound) ?? true,
      soundSuccessOnly: prefs.getBool(kSoundSuccessOnly) ?? true,
      ambientMotionEnabled: prefs.getBool(kAmbient) ?? true,
      forceReduceMotion: reduceRaw == -1 ? null : reduceRaw == 1,
    );
    AzSensory.apply(_prefs);
    _isLoaded = true;
    notifyListeners();
  }

  void _commit(SensoryPreferences next) {
    _prefs = next;
    AzSensory.apply(_prefs);
    notifyListeners();
  }

  Future<void> setHapticsEnabled(bool value) async {
    _commit(SensoryPreferences(
      hapticsEnabled: value,
      soundEnabled: _prefs.soundEnabled,
      soundSuccessOnly: _prefs.soundSuccessOnly,
      ambientMotionEnabled: _prefs.ambientMotionEnabled,
      forceReduceMotion: _prefs.forceReduceMotion,
    ));
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setBool(kHaptics, value);
  }

  Future<void> setSoundEnabled(bool value) async {
    _commit(SensoryPreferences(
      hapticsEnabled: _prefs.hapticsEnabled,
      soundEnabled: value,
      soundSuccessOnly: _prefs.soundSuccessOnly,
      ambientMotionEnabled: _prefs.ambientMotionEnabled,
      forceReduceMotion: _prefs.forceReduceMotion,
    ));
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setBool(kSound, value);
  }

  Future<void> setSoundSuccessOnly(bool value) async {
    _commit(SensoryPreferences(
      hapticsEnabled: _prefs.hapticsEnabled,
      soundEnabled: _prefs.soundEnabled,
      soundSuccessOnly: value,
      ambientMotionEnabled: _prefs.ambientMotionEnabled,
      forceReduceMotion: _prefs.forceReduceMotion,
    ));
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setBool(kSoundSuccessOnly, value);
  }

  Future<void> setAmbientMotionEnabled(bool value) async {
    _commit(SensoryPreferences(
      hapticsEnabled: _prefs.hapticsEnabled,
      soundEnabled: _prefs.soundEnabled,
      soundSuccessOnly: _prefs.soundSuccessOnly,
      ambientMotionEnabled: value,
      forceReduceMotion: _prefs.forceReduceMotion,
    ));
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setBool(kAmbient, value);
  }

  /// Tri-state. `null` clears the override and returns control to the OS.
  Future<void> setForceReduceMotion(bool? value) async {
    _commit(SensoryPreferences(
      hapticsEnabled: _prefs.hapticsEnabled,
      soundEnabled: _prefs.soundEnabled,
      soundSuccessOnly: _prefs.soundSuccessOnly,
      ambientMotionEnabled: _prefs.ambientMotionEnabled,
      forceReduceMotion: value,
    ));
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setInt(kReduceOverride, value == null ? -1 : (value ? 1 : 0));
  }
}

final sensoryProvider = ChangeNotifierProvider<SensoryProvider>((ref) {
  return SensoryProvider();
});
```

> **Why explicit constructors instead of `copyWith`:** `forceReduceMotion` is tri-state, and
> `copyWith({bool? x})` cannot distinguish "leave it alone" from "set it to null". Five setters
> with one shared `_commit` cannot lie.

### Step 2 — Gate `lib/utils/azaman_haptics.dart` (mechanical patch, all bodies preserved)

**Do not replace the file.** TASK-006 may already have shipped richer bodies (two-beat patterns,
`vibration`-package sequences). This step only inserts a gate in front of the existing bodies, so
nothing TASK-006 built is lost.

**2a — insert the gate block immediately after the private constructor.** Find:

```dart
class AzamanHaptics {
  const AzamanHaptics._();
```

Replace with:

```dart
class AzamanHaptics {
  const AzamanHaptics._();

  // ── THE GATE (TASK-026) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  //
  // This file's own header promised a single global off-switch. This is it.
  // `AzSensory.hapticsEnabled` is written by exactly one place —
  // `SensoryProvider._commit` — and defaults to true, so behaviour is
  // unchanged until a user opts out in Settings.
  //
  // Every public method below must call `_allowed` first. A method that
  // skips the gate is a bug: it would vibrate for a user who asked for none.
  static bool get _allowed => AzSensory.hapticsEnabled;
```

…and add the import at the top of the file, after the existing `flutter/services.dart` import:

```dart
import 'package:azaman/providers/sensory_provider.dart';
```

**2b — gate every public method.** For each `static Future<void> <name>(…)` in the file, the body's
**first statement** becomes:

```dart
    if (!_allowed) return Future<void>.value();
```

For any `static void`/non-Future method, the first statement becomes:

```dart
    if (!_allowed) return;
```

The full public surface after this patch is exactly this set — verify each one carries the gate:

| Method | Intent (unchanged from TASK-006 / the original five-rung vocabulary) |
|---|---|
| `nav()` / `navigation()` | every navigation tap: push, bottom-nav, row tile, drawer item (LIGHT) |
| `toggle()` / `selection()` | switch flips, tab switches, picker pulls (selectionClick) |
| `threshold()` | the moment a gesture crosses its commit point — held, fired **once** |
| `confirm()` | "this commits something" (MEDIUM) |
| `commit()` | a financial action that has just succeeded (HEAVY) |
| `success()` | payment sent, order placed, goal reached |
| `warn()` / `warning()` | error / danger / unrecoverable confirm (two-beat) |
| `error()` | hard failure (two-beat, distinct from `warning`) |
| `celebration()` | the reward moment after a real, completed event (see F.5 — never faked) |
| `moneyLanded()` | money received/settled — the "thunk-tick" two-beat |
| `addToCart()` | add-to-tray — two-beat "clack" (30ms delayed second beat) |
| `seatSelected(int index)` | rising intensity per seat so a row feels like a scale |

> If TASK-006 has **not** run yet, this patch still applies — it is a superset. The names in the
> table are the union of the original five (`nav`, `toggle`, `confirm`, `commit`, `success`, `warn`)
> and TASK-006's additions, so neither state is broken by applying it.

**2c — the one non-negotiable rule for callers.** `threshold()` must fire **once per gesture**, and
the gate must be checked **before** the delayed second beat of a two-beat pattern is scheduled. A
two-beat pattern that schedules beat 2 and then returns early still vibrates — that is the classic
"muted the phone and it still buzzed" bug.

```bash
# Verify: every public method in the file is gated.
rg -c "if \(!_allowed\) return" lib/utils/azaman_haptics.dart
rg -n "static (Future<void>|void) [a-zA-Z]+" lib/utils/azaman_haptics.dart | wc -l
# EXPECT: the first count equals the second count (one gate per public method).
```

### Step 3 — NEW `lib/widgets/sensory_preferences_section.dart`

A Level-2 (Plate/Raised) settings block — **not** glass, so it reads as a settings surface rather
than a hero. Five rows, no new package, no dialog: every state change is reversible by another tap.

```dart
// lib/widgets/sensory_preferences_section.dart
// =============================================================================
// SENSORY PREFERENCES SECTION  (TASK-026)
//
// Haptics, sound, "success sounds only", ambient motion, and a tri-state
// reduce-motion control. Level-2 surface on purpose: settings must read as a
// form, not compete with the screen's one hero (assessment §1.3).
//
// Every toggle is a plain M3 Switch styled from AzamanColors. No dialogs.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/sensory_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';
import 'package:azaman/utils/azaman_haptics.dart';

class SensoryPreferencesSection extends ConsumerWidget {
  /// Optional heading override (e.g. "Feel" inside the Settings drawer).
  final String title;

  const SensoryPreferencesSection({super.key, this.title = 'Feel'});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    final colors = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((t) => t.colors));
    final p = ref.watch(sensoryProvider).prefs;

    return Column(
      crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
      children: [
        Padding(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 20, 16, 8),
          child: Text(
            title,
            style: TextStyle(
              color: colors.textTertiary,
              fontSize: 12,
              fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
              letterSpacing: 0.6,
            ),
          ),
        ),
        Container(
          margin: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 16),
          decoration: BoxDecoration(
            color: colors.card,
            borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(14),
            border: Border.all(color: colors.border, width: 0.5),
          ),
          child: Column(
            children: [
              _SensoryRow(
                colors: colors,
                title: 'Haptics',
                subtitle: 'A short tap when something responds',
                value: p.hapticsEnabled,
                onChanged: (v) {
                  ref.read(sensoryProvider).setHapticsEnabled(v);
                  // Fire the acknowledgement AFTER the gate is updated, so
                  // turning haptics on acknowledges itself and turning them off
                  // is silent (the gate is already closed).
                  if (v) AzamanHaptics.toggle();
                },
              ),
              _divider(colors),
              _SensoryRow(
                colors: colors,
                title: 'Sound effects',
                subtitle: 'Success, money received, ticket events',
                value: p.soundEnabled,
                onChanged: (v) => ref.read(sensoryProvider).setSoundEnabled(v),
              ),
              _divider(colors),
              _SensoryRow(
                colors: colors,
                title: 'Success sounds only',
                subtitle: 'Silence the interface tick and the transition whoosh',
                value: p.soundSuccessOnly,
                enabled: p.soundEnabled,
                onChanged: (v) => ref.read(sensoryProvider).setSoundSuccessOnly(v),
              ),
              _divider(colors),
              _SensoryRow(
                colors: colors,
                title: 'Ambient motion',
                subtitle: 'The slow sheen drift on your balance card when idle',
                value: p.ambientMotionEnabled,
                onChanged: (v) => ref.read(sensoryProvider).setAmbientMotionEnabled(v),
              ),
              _divider(colors),
              _ReduceMotionRow(colors: colors, prefs: p, ref: ref),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ],
    );
  }

  Widget _divider(AzamanColors colors) => Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.only(left: 16),
        child: Divider(height: 1, thickness: 0.5, color: colors.divider),
      );
}

class _SensoryRow extends StatelessWidget {
  final AzamanColors colors;
  final String title;
  final String subtitle;
  final bool value;
  final bool enabled;
  final ValueChanged<bool> onChanged;

  const _SensoryRow({
    required this.colors,
    required this.title,
    required this.subtitle,
    required this.value,
    required this.onChanged,
    this.enabled = true,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {

```

Then append `_ReduceMotionRow` and `_Segment` **in the same file**. Flutter has no tri-state switch,
so this is a 3-segment pill — and the three states are genuinely different promises:

```dart
class _ReduceMotionRow extends StatelessWidget {
  final AzamanColors colors;
  final SensoryPreferences prefs;
  final WidgetRef ref;

  const _ReduceMotionRow({
    required this.colors,
    required this.prefs,
    required this.ref,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    //   null  → "follow my phone": the OS reduce-motion setting wins.
    //   true  → always reduce (a user who finds motion uncomfortable).
    //   false → always full motion (a user whose OS flag is on for battery).
    final bool? selected = prefs.forceReduceMotion;

    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 12, 12, 14),
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text('Reduce motion',
              style: TextStyle(
                color: colors.textPrimary,
                fontSize: 14.5,
                fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
              )),
          const SizedBox(height: 2),
          Text('Follows your phone by default. Override it if you prefer.',
              style: TextStyle(color: colors.textTertiary, fontSize: 12, height: 1.35)),
          const SizedBox(height: 10),
          Row(
            children: [
              _Segment(
                colors: colors,
                label: 'Follow phone',
                active: selected == null,
                onTap: () {
                  ref.read(sensoryProvider).setForceReduceMotion(null);
                  AzamanHaptics.selection();
                },
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 8),
              _Segment(
                colors: colors,
                label: 'Always',
                active: selected == true,
                onTap: () {
                  ref.read(sensoryProvider).setForceReduceMotion(true);
                  AzamanHaptics.selection();
                },
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 8),
              _Segment(
                colors: colors,
                label: 'Never',
                active: selected == false,
                onTap: () {
                  ref.read(sensoryProvider).setForceReduceMotion(false);
                  AzamanHaptics.selection();
                },
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

class _Segment extends StatelessWidget {
  final AzamanColors colors;
  final String label;
  final bool active;
  final VoidCallback onTap;

  const _Segment({
    required this.colors,
    required this.label,
    required this.active,
    required this.onTap,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return GestureDetector(
      behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
      onTap: onTap,
      child: AnimatedContainer(
        duration: MotionTokens.control,
        curve: MotionTokens.symmetric,
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 12, vertical: 8),
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: active ? colors.accent.withValues(alpha: 0.14) : colors.softSurface,
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(9),
          border: Border.all(
            color: active ? colors.accent.withValues(alpha: 0.55) : colors.border,
            width: 0.5,
          ),
        ),
        child: Text(
          label,
          style: TextStyle(
            color: active ? colors.accent : colors.textSecondary,
            fontSize: 12,
            fontWeight: active ? FontWeight.w700 : FontWeight.w500,
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

> `MotionTokens.control` (180ms) is the correct step: a segment pill is a **control** state change,
> not a scene change. `emphasized` (350ms) here would be a tempo lie.

## G.2 — TASK-020: `AzSound` — five sounds, one gate, zero new packages

### Why (and the honest constraint)

The assessment's §8.1 is right: sound is the most under-used premium signal in mobile. It is also
the easiest thing to ruin. Two facts shape this spec:

1. **`pubspec.yaml` has no audio package** (verified: no `audioplayers`, no `just_audio`). A.3 rule 6
   forbids introducing one. So this task ships a **two-backend** design: a zero-dependency
   `SystemSoundBackend` that works today, and an asset backend that activates only if the audio
   assets and an approved player exist. Nothing in the app has to change to move between them.
2. **Android/iOS give you exactly two system sounds** (`click`, `alert`). That is enough for the two
   sounds that matter most (a UI tick and a success alert) and is honest on every device. The five
   *named* sounds still exist in the API — three of them simply resolve to the closest system sound
   until real samples land, and `AzSound` reports which backend is live so nobody ships a lie.

**Hard rule (F.5):** sound never plays for a *fabricated* event, never plays when the OS is in
silent/DND mode, and never plays more than once per user action. A success chime on a demo payment
is exactly the kind of thing the money-truth contract exists to prevent.

### Files — NEW

- `lib/services/az_sound.dart`
- `test/az_sound_test.dart`

### Files — MODIFY

- `pubspec.yaml` — **two exact added lines** in the `assets:` list (Step 3). Nothing else.

### Pre-flight

```bash
rg -n "audioplayers|just_audio|soundpool|AudioPlayer" pubspec.yaml
# EXPECT: no output. If a player IS installed, use it as the asset backend and say so
# in the sign-off; the API in Step 1 does not change.

rg -n "SystemSound" lib | wc -l
# EXPECT: 0 — nothing in the app plays a system sound today.

rg -n "assets/audio" pubspec.yaml
# EXPECT: no output (the folder is not declared yet).

ls assets/images assets/animations
# EXPECT: both exist — the `assets/` tree is real, so a new `assets/audio/`
# sibling is consistent with the repo, not an invention.
```

**Asset gate:** create `assets/audio/` and drop in these five files. If any file is missing, the
backend must skip it silently (Step 1's `MediaSoundBackend.load()` catches and no-ops). Do **not**
substitute a different sound for a missing one at runtime without a code change — a "coin" sound
that is really a click is worse than silence.

| Asset | Sound | Character | Duration target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assets/audio/az_tick.mp3` | `AzSound.tick` | soft, dry, no pitch bend | 30-50ms |
| `assets/audio/az_success.mp3` | `AzSound.success` | two ascending notes (perfect 5th) | 350-450ms |
| `assets/audio/az_coin.mp3` | `AzSound.coin` | money received — bright, short decay | 250-350ms |
| `assets/audio/az_rip.mp3` | `AzSound.rip` | paper tear (restaurant ticket / receipt) | 300-400ms |
| `assets/audio/az_whoosh.mp3` | `AzSound.whoosh` | transition air, no tonal centre | 200-300ms |

> Authoring note: keep every file **mono, 44.1kHz, under 30KB**, and normalise to about −16 LUFS.
> Five sounds should add under 150KB to the bundle. A premium app's audio identity is defined by
> what it *refuses* to play, not by how many samples it ships.

### Step 1 — NEW `lib/services/az_sound.dart`

```dart
// lib/services/az_sound.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ SOUND  (TASK-020)
//
// Five named sounds, one gate, zero new packages.
//
// DESIGN
// ------
// `AzSound` is a façade over an [AzSoundBackend]. Two backends are defined:
//
//   SystemSoundBackend  — ships today. Uses Flutter's built-in SystemSound
//                         (`click` / `alert`). No package, no assets, no
//                         platform channel of our own. On Android/iOS those are
//                         the ONLY two sounds the OS exposes, so tick/rip/whoosh
//                         resolve to the closest system sound until real samples
//                         are wired in.
//   SilentSoundBackend  — the default until [AzSound.usePlatformSystemSounds] is
//                         called. Nothing plays on a fresh install before the
//                         shell has decided.
//   MediaSoundBackend   — asset-backed, and deliberately *not* shipped until an
//                         audio player is an approved dependency (A.3 rule 6).
//                         Its seam ([AzSoundMediaPlayer]) is defined here so the
//                         eventual wiring is a one-file change with no call-site
//                         churn.
//
// HONESTY RULES (F.5)
// -------------------
//   * Never play for a fabricated/demo event. A chime on a simulated payment is
//     the exact lie the money-truth contract forbids.
//   * Never play more than once per user action.
//   * Respect the user's gate (`AzSensory`) BEFORE touching the platform.
//   * Never throw. Audio is a garnish; a missing asset must be invisible.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/sensory_provider.dart';

/// The five sounds the product is allowed to make.
enum AzSoundId { tick, success, coin, rip, whoosh }

/// What is actually producing sound right now. Surfaced so screens, tests and
/// the sign-off can state the truth instead of assuming.
enum AzSoundBackendKind { silent, system, mediaAssets }

abstract class AzSoundBackend {
  AzSoundBackendKind get kind;
  Future<void> preload(Set<AzSoundId> ids);
  Future<void> play(AzSoundId id);
  void dispose();
}

/// Does nothing, forever. The default.
class SilentSoundBackend implements AzSoundBackend {
  const SilentSoundBackend();

  @override
  AzSoundBackendKind get kind => AzSoundBackendKind.silent;

  @override
  Future<void> preload(Set<AzSoundId> ids) async {}

  @override
  Future<void> play(AzSoundId id) async {}

  @override
  void dispose() {}
}

/// Zero-dependency backend: Flutter's built-in system sounds.
class SystemSoundBackend implements AzSoundBackend {
  const SystemSoundBackend();

  @override
  AzSoundBackendKind get kind => AzSoundBackendKind.system;

  /// The exact mapping, exposed as a pure function so it can be unit-tested
  /// without touching a platform channel.
  static SystemSoundType? systemTypeFor(AzSoundId id) {
    switch (id) {
      case AzSoundId.tick:
        return SystemSoundType.click;
      case AzSoundId.rip:
        return SystemSoundType.click;
      case AzSoundId.whoosh:
        return SystemSoundType.click;
      case AzSoundId.success:
        return SystemSoundType.alert;
      case AzSoundId.coin:
        return SystemSoundType.alert;
    }
  }

  @override
  Future<void> preload(Set<AzSoundId> ids) async {
    // System sounds are preloaded by the OS. Intentionally empty.
  }

  @override
  Future<void> play(AzSoundId id) async {
    final type = systemTypeFor(id);
    if (type == null) return;
    try {
      await SystemSound.play(type);
    } on PlatformException {
      // Some devices/emulators have no system-sound channel. Stay silent.
    } on MissingPluginException {
      // Unit tests and desktop: silent by design.
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {}
}

/// The seam a real audio player plugs into.
///
/// No audio package is installed today (A.3 rule 6). When one is approved,
/// implement this interface in a single new file and pass it to
/// [AzSound.registerAssetBackend] from the app shell. No call site changes.
abstract class AzSoundMediaPlayer {
  Future<void> load(String assetPath);
  Future<void> play();
  Future<void> stop();
  void dispose();
}

/// Asset-backed backend. Activated only when a player is injected.
class MediaSoundBackend implements AzSoundBackend {
  final AzSoundMediaPlayer Function() _createPlayer;
  final Map<AzSoundId, AzSoundMediaPlayer> _players = {};

  MediaSoundBackend(this._createPlayer);

  @override
  AzSoundBackendKind get kind => AzSoundBackendKind.mediaAssets;

  /// The one place asset paths are written down.
  static const Map<AzSoundId, String> assetPaths = {
    AzSoundId.tick: 'assets/audio/az_tick.mp3',
    AzSoundId.success: 'assets/audio/az_success.mp3',
    AzSoundId.coin: 'assets/audio/az_coin.mp3',
    AzSoundId.rip: 'assets/audio/az_rip.mp3',
    AzSoundId.whoosh: 'assets/audio/az_whoosh.mp3',
  };

  /// Loads every sound it can and silently skips every one it cannot. A missing
  /// asset is a content gap, not a crash — and skipping is visible in
  /// `AzSound.loadedIds`, so the sign-off can be honest about it.
  @override
  Future<void> preload(Set<AzSoundId> ids) async {
    for (final id in ids) {
      if (_players.containsKey(id)) continue;
      final path = assetPaths[id];
      if (path == null) continue;
      final player = _createPlayer();
      try {
        await player.load(path);
        _players[id] = player;
      } catch (_) {
        player.dispose(); // asset absent or unreadable — stay silent for this id
      }
    }
  }

  Set<AzSoundId> get loadedIds => _players.keys.toSet();

  @override
  Future<void> play(AzSoundId id) async {
    final player = _players[id];
    if (player == null) return;
    try {
      await player.play();
    } catch (_) {
      // Never surface an audio failure.
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    for (final p in _players.values) {
      p.dispose();
    }
    _players.clear();
  }
}

/// The façade every screen calls. Static by design: sound fires from callbacks
/// that have no guaranteed BuildContext, exactly like haptics.
class AzSound {
  const AzSound._();

  static AzSoundBackend _backend = const SilentSoundBackend();
  static bool _preloaded = false;

  /// The minimum gap between two plays of the SAME sound. A double-tap must not
  /// produce a double tick — that is the single most common way app sound reads
  /// as cheap.
  static const Duration minRepeatGap = Duration(milliseconds: 60);

  static final Map<AzSoundId, DateTime> _lastPlayed = {};

  static AzSoundBackendKind get backendKind => _backend.kind;

  /// True when a real sound can play. Screens may use this to decide whether to
  /// show a "sound" affordance at all.
  static bool get isAudible => _backend.kind != AzSoundBackendKind.silent;

  /// Ids the active backend actually loaded (media backend only).
  static Set<AzSoundId> get loadedIds =>
      _backend is MediaSoundBackend ? (_backend as MediaSoundBackend).loadedIds : const {};

  /// Called ONCE from the app shell. Safe to call repeatedly.
  static void usePlatformSystemSounds() {
    _swap(const SystemSoundBackend());
  }

  /// Swap in an asset backend (or a test double).
  static void registerAssetBackend(AzSoundBackend backend) {
    _swap(backend);
  }

  static void _swap(AzSoundBackend next) {
    _backend.dispose();
    _backend = next;
    _preloaded = false;
    _lastPlayed.clear();
  }

  /// Warms the backend. Non-blocking by design — never await this on a build path.
  static Future<void> ensureReady() async {
    if (_preloaded) return;
    _preloaded = true;
    try {
      await _backend.preload(AzSoundId.values.toSet());
    } catch (_) {
      // A preload failure must never break a screen.
    }
  }

  /// The gate. Order matters: user preference first, then de-duplication, then
  /// the platform. [essential] sounds (success / coin / rip) are the ones the
  /// user opted into with "success sounds only"; tick and whoosh are garnish.
  static Future<void> _play(AzSoundId id, {required bool essential}) async {
    if (!AzSensory.soundEnabled) return;
    if (AzSensory.soundSuccessOnly && !essential) return;

    final now = DateTime.now();
    final last = _lastPlayed[id];
    if (last != null && now.difference(last) < minRepeatGap) return;
    _lastPlayed[id] = now;

    try {
      await _backend.play(id);
    } catch (_) {
      // Silence is always an acceptable outcome.
    }
  }

  // ── The five sounds ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  /// Interface garnish — silenced by "success sounds only".
  static Future<void> tick({bool essential = false}) =>
      _play(AzSoundId.tick, essential: essential);

  /// A real, completed success (never a demo/simulated one). See F.5.
  static Future<void> success() => _play(AzSoundId.success, essential: true);

  /// Money received or settled — pairs with `AzamanHaptics.moneyLanded()`.
  static Future<void> coin() => _play(AzSoundId.coin, essential: true);

  /// Paper tear — restaurant ticket, retail receipt, escrow unseal.
  static Future<void> rip() => _play(AzSoundId.rip, essential: true);

  /// Scene change air. Rare by design; never on a tab switch.
  static Future<void> whoosh() => _play(AzSoundId.whoosh, essential: false);

  /// Test-only: clears the debounce table so a test can play the same sound twice.
  static void resetDebounceForTest() => _lastPlayed.clear();
}
```

> `tick()` takes an `essential` flag rather than being hard-coded non-essential, so a screen can
> promote it in exactly one place if it turns out to matter (for example, the amount-stage keypad,
> where a tick per digit is the sound the user *expects*).

### Step 2 — Wire the shell and pair sound with haptics (grep-gated, no guessing)

**2a — shell init.** In `lib/main.dart`, inside `_bootstrap()`, after the existing
`ErrorWidget.builder = (FlutterErrorDetails details) { … };` block (L144-163) and before
`SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(...)` (L165), insert:

```dart

  // Warm it off the critical path so the first real success is not late.
  AzSound.usePlatformSystemSounds();
  unawaited(AzSound.ensureReady());
```

Add the imports next to the existing package imports in the same file:

```dart

import 'dart:async'; // for unawaited()
```

> If `dart:async` is already imported, use it. `unawaited` is in `dart:async`.

**2b — the pairing rule.** Sound is never added on its own. It is added **at the exact site where the
matching haptic already fires**, because that site is already proven to be the real, user-visible
moment. Enumerate those sites:

```bash
rg -n "AzamanHaptics\.(success|commit|moneyLanded|addToCart|celebration)\(" lib
```

For each hit, add **one** line directly after the haptic call, per this table:

| Existing haptic call | Line to add | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `AzamanHaptics.success()` | `AzSound.success();` | order placed, goal reached, real payment settled |
| `AzamanHaptics.moneyLanded()` | `AzSound.coin();` | money received/settled — the two cues must land together |
| `AzamanHaptics.commit()` | `AzSound.success();` | final commit on a money action |
| `AzamanHaptics.addToCart()` | `AzSound.tick();` | tray catch — deliberately quiet (garnish) |
| `AzamanHaptics.celebration()` | `AzSound.success();` | the reward moment — **only** after a real completion |
| paper-tear / receipt / unseal sites (TASK-013/016) | `AzSound.rip();` | the rip *is* the sound; fire it with the painter's tear, not the tap |
| route morph sites (NEW-J) | `AzSound.whoosh();` | scene change only — never on a tab switch |

> The table's third column is the honesty check. If you cannot name the *real* event the sound
> accompanies, do not add the sound.

```bash
rg -n -B3 "AzSound\.(success|coin)\(" lib | rg -n -i "demo|simulate|fake|placeholder"
```

### Step 4 — NEW `test/az_sound_test.dart`

```dart
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/sensory_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/services/az_sound.dart';

/// Records what the façade asked for, so the *gate* can be tested without a
/// platform channel or an asset.
class _RecordingBackend implements AzSoundBackend {
  final List<AzSoundId> played = [];
  Set<AzSoundId> preloaded = {};

  @override
  AzSoundBackendKind get kind => AzSoundBackendKind.mediaAssets;

  @override
  Future<void> preload(Set<AzSoundId> ids) async => preloaded = ids;

  @override
  Future<void> play(AzSoundId id) async => played.add(id);

  @override
  void dispose() {}
}

void main() {
  TestWidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  late _RecordingBackend recorder;

  setUp(() {
    recorder = _RecordingBackend();
    AzSound.registerAssetBackend(recorder);
    AzSound.resetDebounceForTest();
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences());
  });

  tearDown(() {
    AzSound.registerAssetBackend(const SilentSoundBackend());
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences());
  });

  test('the user gate wins over everything', () async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(
      soundEnabled: false,
      soundSuccessOnly: false,
    ));
    await AzSound.success();
    await AzSound.coin();
    await AzSound.tick();
    expect(recorder.played, isEmpty);
  });

  test('success-only mode silences garnish but keeps real events', () async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(
      soundEnabled: true,
      soundSuccessOnly: true,
    ));
    await AzSound.tick();
    await AzSound.whoosh();
    expect(recorder.played, isEmpty, reason: 'tick/whoosh are garnish');

    await AzSound.success();
    await AzSound.coin();
    await AzSound.rip();
    expect(recorder.played,
        [AzSoundId.success, AzSoundId.coin, AzSoundId.rip]);
  });

  test('full sound mode plays everything, including an essential tick', () async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(
      soundEnabled: true,
      soundSuccessOnly: false,
    ));
    await AzSound.tick();
    await AzSound.whoosh();
    await AzSound.tick(essential: true);
    expect(recorder.played, [AzSoundId.tick, AzSoundId.whoosh, AzSoundId.tick]);
  });

  test('a repeat inside minRepeatGap is dropped (no double-tick)', () async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(
      soundEnabled: true,
      soundSuccessOnly: false,
    ));
    await AzSound.tick();
    await AzSound.tick(); // immediate second call — must be swallowed
    expect(recorder.played, [AzSoundId.tick]);

    AzSound.resetDebounceForTest();
    await AzSound.tick();
    expect(recorder.played, [AzSoundId.tick, AzSoundId.tick]);
  });

  test('different ids never block each other', () async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(
      soundEnabled: true,
      soundSuccessOnly: false,
    ));
    await AzSound.tick();
    await AzSound.whoosh();
    expect(recorder.played, [AzSoundId.tick, AzSoundId.whoosh]);
  });

  test('system backend maps all five ids to a real system sound', () {
    for (final id in AzSoundId.values) {
      expect(SystemSoundBackend.systemTypeFor(id), isNotNull,
          reason: '$id must resolve to click or alert');
    }
    expect(SystemSoundBackend.systemTypeFor(AzSoundId.tick),
        SystemSoundType.click);
    expect(SystemSoundBackend.systemTypeFor(AzSoundId.success),
        SystemSoundType.alert);
    expect(SystemSoundBackend.systemTypeFor(AzSoundId.coin),
        SystemSoundType.alert);
  });

  test('ensureReady preloads every id exactly once', () async {
    await AzSound.ensureReady();
    await AzSound.ensureReady();
    expect(recorder.preloaded.length, AzSoundId.values.length);
  });

  test('a missing asset is skipped, not thrown', () async {
    final backend = MediaSoundBackend(() => _FailingPlayer());
    await backend.preload(AzSoundId.values.toSet());
    expect(backend.loadedIds, isEmpty);
    await backend.play(AzSoundId.success); // must not throw
    backend.dispose();
  });

  test('media backend records only the ids it could load', () async {
    final backend = MediaSoundBackend(() => _OkPlayer());
    await backend.preload({AzSoundId.tick, AzSoundId.success});
    expect(backend.loadedIds, {AzSoundId.tick, AzSoundId.success});
    backend.dispose();
  });
}

class _FailingPlayer implements AzSoundMediaPlayer {
  @override
  Future<void> load(String assetPath) async => throw Exception('asset missing');
  @override
  Future<void> play() async {}
  @override
  Future<void> stop() async {}
  @override
  void dispose() {}
}

class _OkPlayer implements AzSoundMediaPlayer {
  @override
  Future<void> load(String assetPath) async {}
  @override
  Future<void> play() async {}
  @override
  Future<void> stop() async {}
  @override
  void dispose() {}
}
```

## G.3 — TASK-023: Designed error / empty / offline states

### Why

The assessment (§8.3, §8.4, §8.5) names three failures that are cheap to fix and disproportionately
visible, because each one is a *whole screen the user stares at with nothing else on it*:

1. **Error surfaces don't speak Azaman.** `lib/main.dart` L144-163 installs an `ErrorWidget.builder`
   that renders `Material(color: Color(0xFF1A1A2E))` — a hardcoded hex in the one file that otherwise
   carefully avoids them. There is no retry, no way forward, and the copy blames the user
   ("Pull down to refresh, or restart the app."). This is the *only* screen in the app that isn't
   designed, and it appears precisely when the user is already frustrated.
2. **Empty states are an icon in a circle** (`lib/widgets/azaman_empty_state.dart`, verified: a
   `Container` with `accent @6%`, a `textTertiary` icon, two `Text`s, a `TextButton`). It is
   consistent — which is the whole win it currently offers. It has no drawing, no voice, no entrance.
3. **Offline is a bar that pushes content.** `lib/widgets/azaman_connectivity_banner.dart` (verified)
   overlays a 12px-margin pill with a 35%-alpha glow shadow and the subtitle *"Showing your last
   loaded data. Some actions are paused."* It is honest but loud; the assessment asks for a 24px
   hairline instead, with a "last updated" chip on stale data rather than a permanent bar.

### Files — NEW

- `lib/widgets/az_error_surface.dart`
- `lib/widgets/offline_hairline.dart`
- `lib/widgets/az_state_illustration.dart`
- `test/widgets/az_error_surface_test.dart`
- `test/widgets/offline_hairline_test.dart`

- `lib/main.dart` — replace the `ErrorWidget.builder` body (L144-163).
