### Step 1 — NEW `lib/widgets/az_state_illustration.dart`

Four hand-drawn states. The assessment's point (§8.3) is that an empty state is the *highest-attention
surface in the app* — nothing competes with it — so it deserves a drawing, not an icon. Four scenes,
one entry widget, zero assets, zero packages.

```dart
// lib/widgets/az_state_illustration.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ STATE ILLUSTRATION  (TASK-023)
//
// A drawn state, not an icon in a circle. Five scenes, all vector, all painted
// from the live theme so they re-tint with accents and both brightnesses.
//
// Why draw instead of ship PNGs: the app already refuses the asset pipeline for
// anything that must tint perfectly (see the seat-canvas painter). A drawing
// costs nothing at every density, and it can draw itself on entry.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';

enum AzStateScene { emptyBox, offline, error, search, receipt }

class AzStateIllustration extends StatelessWidget {
  final AzStateScene scene;
  final AzamanColors colors;
  final double size;

  /// 0 → 1 entrance progress. Animate this from the caller, or leave it at 1.
  final double progress;

  const AzStateIllustration({
    super.key,
    required this.scene,
    required this.colors,
    this.size = 96,
    this.progress = 1.0,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return SizedBox(
      width: size,
      height: size,
      child: CustomPaint(
        painter: _AzStatePainter(
          scene: scene,
          colors: colors,
          progress: progress.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

class _AzStatePainter extends CustomPainter {
  final AzStateScene scene;
  final AzamanColors colors;
  final double progress;

  const _AzStatePainter({
    required this.scene,
    required this.colors,
    required this.progress,
  });

  @override
  void paint(Canvas canvas, Size size) {
    // Everything is drawn inside a 100x100 box and then scaled, so the painter
    // is resolution-independent and every scene shares one coordinate space.
    canvas.save();
    canvas.scale(size.width / 100.0, size.height / 100.0);
    switch (scene) {
      case AzStateScene.emptyBox:
        _drawBox(canvas);
        break;
      case AzStateScene.offline:
        _drawOffline(canvas);
        break;
      case AzStateScene.error:
        _drawError(canvas);
        break;
      case AzStateScene.search:
        _drawSearch(canvas);
        break;
      case AzStateScene.receipt:
        _drawReceipt(canvas);
        break;
    }
    canvas.restore();
  }

  Paint _stroke(double width, Color color, {bool soft = false}) => Paint()
    ..style = PaintingStyle.stroke
    ..strokeWidth = width
    ..strokeCap = StrokeCap.round
    ..strokeJoin = StrokeJoin.round
    ..color = color.withValues(alpha: soft ? 0.45 : 1.0);

  Paint _fill(Color color, double alpha) => Paint()
    ..style = PaintingStyle.fill
    ..color = color.withValues(alpha: alpha);

  /// Progressive reveal: draw only the first `progress` fraction of each path's
  /// length. All geometry here is polylines/arcs, so this is exact and cheap —
  /// and it means every scene "draws itself" with no extra code per scene.
  Path _progressive(Path path) {
    if (progress >= 1.0) return path;
    final out = Path();
    for (final metric in path.computeMetrics()) {
      out.addPath(metric.extractPath(0, metric.length * progress), Offset.zero);
    }
    return out;
  }

  void _drawBox(Canvas canvas) {
    final lid = Path()
      ..moveTo(22, 42)
      ..lineTo(50, 30)
      ..lineTo(78, 42)
      ..lineTo(50, 54)
      ..close();
    final body = Path()
      ..moveTo(22, 42)
      ..lineTo(22, 72)
      ..lineTo(50, 84)
      ..lineTo(78, 72)
      ..lineTo(78, 42);
    final spine = Path()
      ..moveTo(50, 54)
      ..lineTo(50, 84);
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(lid), _stroke(2.5, colors.accent));
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(body), _stroke(2.5, colors.textTertiary));
    canvas.drawPath(
        _progressive(spine), _stroke(1.5, colors.textTertiary, soft: true));
  }

  void _drawOffline(Canvas canvas) {
    final cloud = Path()
      ..moveTo(30, 62)
      ..arcToPoint(const Offset(38, 46), radius: const Radius.circular(12))
      ..arcToPoint(const Offset(62, 44), radius: const Radius.circular(16))
      ..arcToPoint(const Offset(72, 62), radius: const Radius.circular(13))
      ..close();
    final slash = Path()
      ..moveTo(22, 78)
      ..lineTo(78, 26);
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(cloud), _stroke(2.5, colors.textTertiary));
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(slash), _stroke(3.0, colors.warning));
    canvas.drawCircle(const Offset(50, 84), 2.5, _fill(colors.warning, 0.8));
  }

  void _drawError(Canvas canvas) {
    final shield = Path()
      ..moveTo(50, 22)
      ..lineTo(74, 32)
      ..lineTo(74, 56)
      ..quadraticBezierTo(72, 76, 50, 84)
      ..quadraticBezierTo(28, 76, 26, 56)
      ..lineTo(26, 32)
      ..close();
    final bang = Path()
      ..moveTo(50, 40)
      ..lineTo(50, 60);
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(shield), _stroke(2.5, colors.danger));
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(bang), _stroke(3.0, colors.danger));
    canvas.drawCircle(const Offset(50, 69), 2.6, _fill(colors.danger, 1.0));
  }

  void _drawSearch(Canvas canvas) {
    final ring = Path()
      ..addOval(Rect.fromCircle(center: const Offset(44, 44), radius: 20));
    final handle = Path()
      ..moveTo(59, 59)
      ..lineTo(76, 76);
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(ring), _stroke(2.5, colors.textTertiary));
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(handle), _stroke(3.0, colors.accent));
    canvas.drawCircle(const Offset(44, 44), 3.0, _fill(colors.accent, 0.5));
  }

  void _drawReceipt(Canvas canvas) {
    final paper = Path()
      ..moveTo(32, 22)
      ..lineTo(68, 22)
      ..lineTo(68, 70)
      ..lineTo(62, 76)
      ..lineTo(56, 70)
      ..lineTo(50, 76)
      ..lineTo(44, 70)
      ..lineTo(38, 76)
      ..lineTo(32, 70)
      ..close();
    canvas.drawPath(_progressive(paper), _stroke(2.5, colors.textTertiary));
    for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
      final y = 34.0 + i * 10;
      final line = Path()
        ..moveTo(40, y)
        ..lineTo(i == 2 ? 54 : 60, y);
      canvas.drawPath(
          _progressive(line), _stroke(1.5, colors.textTertiary, soft: true));
    }
  }

  @override
  bool shouldRepaint(covariant _AzStatePainter old) =>
      old.scene != scene ||
      old.progress != progress ||
      old.colors.accent != colors.accent ||
      old.colors.isDark != colors.isDark;
}
```

> `progress` means the drawing *develops* rather than blinking on. TASK-022's `AzResolve` is the
> consumer that animates it; at `progress: 1.0` it is simply drawn. Use `MotionTokens.emphasized`
> (350ms) for the entrance — 900ms of drawing on an empty state is a delay, not a delight — and snap
> straight to 1.0 under reduced motion.

### Step 2 — NEW `lib/widgets/az_error_surface.dart`

```dart
// lib/widgets/az_error_surface.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ ERROR SURFACE  (TASK-023)
//
// The designed replacement for two things:
//   1. `main.dart`'s `ErrorWidget.builder` (a hardcoded #1A1A2E Material box).
//   2. Ad-hoc "something went wrong" bodies inside screens.
//
// Rules it enforces:
//   * A Level-2 surface (Plate/Raised), never a bare hardcoded colour.
//   * One human sentence + one action. No stack traces, no blame.
//   * A way FORWARD: retry, and (when the data is merely stale) continue offline.
//   * Never claims the retry worked. It calls the callback and gets out of the way.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';
import 'package:azaman/utils/azaman_haptics.dart';
import 'package:azaman/widgets/az_state_illustration.dart';

class AzErrorSurface extends StatelessWidget {
  /// One sentence, in the product's voice. Never a raw exception string.
  final String message;

  /// Optional second line: what the user can still do.
  final String? hint;

  final VoidCallback? onRetry;

  /// Shown only when cached data exists — otherwise "continue offline" is a lie.
  final VoidCallback? onContinueOffline;

  final AzStateScene scene;

  /// Set false when this is rendered inside a list cell rather than a page.
  final bool expand;

  const AzErrorSurface({
    super.key,
    required this.message,
    this.hint,
    this.onRetry,
    this.onContinueOffline,
    this.scene = AzStateScene.error,
    this.expand = true,
  });

  /// Used by `main.dart`'s framework error hook. Deliberately generic: a build
  /// error has no user-meaningful detail, and inventing one would be a lie.
  factory AzErrorSurface.fromFramework({Key? key, VoidCallback? onRetry}) =>
      AzErrorSurface(
        key: key,
        message: 'This part of Azaman did not load.',
        hint: 'Your data is safe. Try again, or go back and continue.',
        onRetry: onRetry,
        scene: AzStateScene.error,
      );

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final colors = Theme.of(context).brightness == Brightness.dark
        ? ThemeProvider.getColors(AzamanTheme.dark)
        : ThemeProvider.getColors(AzamanTheme.light);

    return Container(
      width: double.infinity,
      color: colors.background,
      padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 28, vertical: 32),
      child: Center(
        child: ConstrainedBox(
          constraints: const BoxConstraints(maxWidth: 360),
          child: Column(
            mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
            children: [
              AzStateIllustration(scene: scene, colors: colors, size: 92),
              const SizedBox(height: 18),
              Text(
                message,
                textAlign: TextAlign.center,
                style: TextStyle(
                  color: colors.textPrimary,
                  fontSize: 16,
                  fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
                  height: 1.35,
                ),
              ),
              if (hint != null) ...[
                const SizedBox(height: 8),
                Text(
                  hint!,
                  textAlign: TextAlign.center,
                  style: TextStyle(
                    color: colors.textTertiary,
                    fontSize: 13,
                    height: 1.45,
                  ),
                ),
              ],
              if (onRetry != null) ...[
                const SizedBox(height: 20),
                _Action(
                  colors: colors,
                  label: 'Try again',
                  primary: true,
                  onTap: () {
                    AzamanHaptics.confirm();
                    onRetry!();
                  },
                ),
              ],
              if (onContinueOffline != null) ...[
                const SizedBox(height: 10),
                _Action(
                  colors: colors,
                  label: 'Continue offline',
                  primary: false,
                  onTap: () {
                    AzamanHaptics.navigation();
                    onContinueOffline!();
                  },
                ),
              ],
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

class _Action extends StatelessWidget {
  final AzamanColors colors;
  final String label;
  final bool primary;
  final VoidCallback onTap;

  const _Action({
    required this.colors,
    required this.label,
    required this.primary,
    required this.onTap,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return GestureDetector(
      behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
      onTap: onTap,
      child: AnimatedContainer(
        duration: MotionTokens.control,
        curve: MotionTokens.symmetric,
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 22, vertical: 12),
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: primary ? colors.accent : Colors.transparent,
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(12),
          border: Border.all(
            color: primary ? colors.accent : colors.border,
            width: primary ? 0 : 0.5,
          ),
        ),
        child: Text(
          label,
          style: TextStyle(
            color: primary ? (colors.isDark ? Colors.black : Colors.white) : colors.textSecondary,
            fontSize: 14,
            fontWeight: FontWeight.w700,
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

> `AzErrorSurface.fromFramework` resolves `AzamanColors` from `Theme.of(context).brightness` rather
> than `ref.watch`, because the widget it replaces runs **outside** the app's normal widget context
> during a build failure — a `ConsumerWidget` there can throw a second time. That is deliberate.

### Step 3 — Replace `main.dart`'s framework error hook

Find (currently L144-163):

```dart
  ErrorWidget.builder = (FlutterErrorDetails details) {
    return const Material(
      color: Color(0xFF1A1A2E),
      child: Center(
        child: Padding(
          padding: EdgeInsets.all(32),
          child: Column(
            mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
            children: [
              Icon(Icons.error_outline, color: Colors.redAccent, size: 48),
              SizedBox(height: 16),
              Text('Something went wrong', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.white, fontSize: 18, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold)),
              SizedBox(height: 8),
              Text('Pull down to refresh, or restart the app.', style: TextStyle(color: Colors.white54, fontSize: 13)),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  };
```

Replace with:

```dart
  // A build failure is the ONE screen with nothing else on it — and the screen a
  // user sees when they are already frustrated. It is designed like the rest of
  // the app now: theme-derived colours, one human sentence, a way forward. The
  // old body hardcoded #1A1A2E and told the user to restart the app.
  ErrorWidget.builder = (FlutterErrorDetails details) {
    return AzErrorSurface.fromFramework(
      onRetry: () {
        // There is no safe "re-run the failed build" from here. In debug this
        // nudges the tree; in release the user leaves via the OS back gesture,
        // which is exactly why the copy reads "or go back".
        final previous = _lastFrameworkError.value;
        _lastFrameworkError.value = null;
        _lastFrameworkError.value = previous;
      },
    );
  };
```

Add the import next to the other `package:azaman/...` imports in `main.dart`:

```dart
import 'package:azaman/widgets/az_error_surface.dart';
```

rg -n "AzErrorSurface" lib/main.dart | wc -l
# EXPECT: 2 (one import + one use).

### Step 4 — NEW `lib/widgets/offline_hairline.dart` + swap the bar for it

The banner is honest but loud: a 12px-margin pill with a coloured shadow, permanently floating over
the content the user is reading. The assessment asks for a 24px hairline — same information, a tenth
of the noise — and the "last updated" truth belongs on the data that is actually stale.

```dart
// lib/widgets/offline_hairline.dart
// =============================================================================
// OFFLINE HAIRLINE  (TASK-023)
//
// 24px tall, edge-to-edge, no shadow, no icon, no card. It changes colour and
// nothing else moves — the app never re-lays out because the radio dropped.
//
// Why: the previous banner was a floating pill with a 35%-alpha glow that sat on
// top of content. A premium app states the truth quietly and keeps working.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

class OfflineHairline extends StatelessWidget {
  final bool offline;
  final bool justReconnected;

  const OfflineHairline({
    super.key,
    required this.offline,
    this.justReconnected = false,
  });

  /// 24 logical pixels: tall enough to read, too short to be a bar.
  static const double height = 24;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final bool visible = offline || justReconnected;
    final Color background = offline
        ? const Color(0xFFFFF3D6)
        : const Color(0xFFDFF5E6);
    final Color foreground = offline
        ? const Color(0xFF7A5B00)
        : const Color(0xFF0B5B33);
    final String label =
        offline ? 'Offline — showing your last update' : 'Back online';

    return AnimatedContainer(
      duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 220),
      curve: Curves.easeOutCubic,
      height: visible ? height : 0,
      width: double.infinity,
      color: visible ? background : Colors.transparent,
      alignment: Alignment.center,
      child: ClipRect(
        child: AnimatedOpacity(
          duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 180),
          opacity: visible ? 1 : 0,
          child: Text(
            label,
            maxLines: 1,
            overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
            textAlign: TextAlign.center,
            style: TextStyle(
              color: foreground,
              fontSize: 11.5,
              fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
              letterSpacing: 0.2,
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

## G.4 — TASK-022: Skeleton → content choreography (`AzResolve`)

### Why

The assessment (§8.2) is precise: skeletons exist (`az_skeleton.dart`, `skeleton_loader.dart`,
`premium_shimmer.dart`, a storefront skeleton) but they **swap** instead of **resolving**. Content
should arrive *in the order the skeleton drew it*, so the screen looks like a photograph developing in
a darkroom rather than a light switch.

Two concrete defects found in the verified source:

- `az_skeleton.dart` L23-31 hardcodes its shimmer colours (`0xFF2A2A3E`, `0xFF3A3A5E`, `0xFFE8E8E8`,
  `0xFFF5F5F5`) — four hex literals that ignore the theme. On the **default light theme** the
  skeleton renders grey-blue against a warm-white page: off-brand on the most-used theme.
- `skeleton_loader.dart` L43 hardcodes `Duration(milliseconds: 1200)` instead of `MotionTokens.ambient`
  (900ms), so skeletons run at a tempo nothing else in the app uses.

### Files — NEW

- `lib/widgets/az_resolve_transition.dart`
- `test/az_resolve_transition_test.dart`

### Files — MODIFY

- `lib/widgets/az_skeleton.dart` — theme-derived colours (Step 2).
- `lib/widgets/skeleton_loader.dart` — `MotionTokens.ambient` (Step 2).
- Adoption is **grep-gated and opportunistic** (Step 3). No repo-wide sweep (A.3 rule 1).

### Step 1 — NEW `lib/widgets/az_resolve_transition.dart`

```dart
// lib/widgets/az_resolve_transition.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ RESOLVE TRANSITION  (TASK-022)
//
// A skeleton should RESOLVE into content, not swap with it.
//
// The screen reports an [AzResolvePhase] while loading. When that flips to
// `resolved`, this widget plays one short entrance: each block fades and lifts
// into place in draw order, staggered by MotionTokens.staggerDelay and capped by
// MotionTokens.staggerMax, so a 20-row list cannot take 800ms.
//
// Reduced motion: the entrance collapses to ONE 180ms cross-fade, no stagger, no
// lift. The information survives; the choreography does not.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';
import 'package:azaman/utils/azaman_haptics.dart';

enum AzResolvePhase { loading, resolved }

class AzResolveTransition extends StatefulWidget {
  /// The content to reveal.
  final Widget child;

  /// Position in the draw order. 0 is the first thing the skeleton drew.
  final int index;

  /// Flips to [AzResolvePhase.resolved] when the data has arrived.
  final AzResolvePhase phase;

  /// Suppress the entrance entirely (e.g. a tab the user is returning to).
  final bool skipEntrance;

  /// Fire a haptic when the FIRST block resolves. Only pass true for index 0,
  /// and only where the arrival is a result the user actually waited for.
  final bool announce;

  const AzResolveTransition({
    super.key,
    required this.child,
    required this.phase,
    this.index = 0,
    this.skipEntrance = false,
    this.announce = false,
  });

  @override
  State<AzResolveTransition> createState() => _AzResolveTransitionState();
}

class _AzResolveTransitionState extends State<AzResolveTransition>
    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  late final AnimationController _controller;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    final resolved = widget.phase == AzResolvePhase.resolved;
    final shouldPlay = resolved && !widget.skipEntrance;
    _controller = AnimationController(
      vsync: this,
      duration: MotionTokens.emphasized, // 350ms per block
      value: shouldPlay ? 0.0 : 1.0,
    );
    if (shouldPlay) {
      // MediaQuery must NOT be read from initState (F-060). The entrance needs
      // MediaQuery.disableAnimations, so it waits for the first frame.
      WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
        if (!mounted) return;
        _playEntrance();
      });
    }
  }

  @override
  void didUpdateWidget(covariant AzResolveTransition old) {
    super.didUpdateWidget(old);
    final wasLoading = old.phase == AzResolvePhase.loading;
    final isResolved = widget.phase == AzResolvePhase.resolved;
    if (wasLoading && isResolved && !widget.skipEntrance) _playEntrance();
  }

  void _playEntrance() {
    final delay = MotionTokens.staggerDelay(widget.index);
    if (MotionTokens.accessibleDuration(context, delay) == Duration.zero) {
      // Reduced motion: land immediately, no stagger, no lift.
      _controller.value = 1.0;
      return;
    }
    Future<void>.delayed(delay, () {
      if (!mounted) return;
      _controller.forward(from: 0.0);
      if (widget.announce && widget.index == 0) {
        AzamanHaptics.success();
      }
    });
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _controller.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    if (MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations) {
      // A designed reduced-motion path, not a missing animation.
      return AnimatedOpacity(
        duration: MotionTokens.control, // 180ms cross-fade
        opacity: widget.phase == AzResolvePhase.resolved ? 1.0 : 0.001,
        child: widget.child,
      );
    }

    return AnimatedBuilder(
      animation: _controller,
      child: widget.child,
      builder: (context, child) {
        final t = MotionTokens.enter.transform(_controller.value);
        return Opacity(
          opacity: t,
          // 6px, not 24px: the block ARRIVES, it does not fly in.
          child: Transform.translate(offset: Offset(0, (1 - t) * 6), child: child),
        );
      },
    );
  }
}
```

### Step 2 — De-brand the skeletons (two exact edits)

**2a — `az_skeleton.dart`: theme-derived shimmer.** Replace the class declaration:

> `ConsumerWidget` does not change any call site: `AzSkeleton(...)` still constructs the same way, and
> the whole app is already under a `ProviderScope`. It is the smallest change that lets the widget
> read `AzamanColors` (A.3 rule 3 allows this — no parameter changes).

Then replace the `build` method (currently L19-35) with:

```dart
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    // Theme-derived. The previous version hardcoded 0xFF2A2A3E / 0xFF3A3A5E /
    // 0xFFE8E8E8 / 0xFFF5F5F5, which made skeletons render grey-blue on the
    // DEFAULT LIGHT THEME — four literals that made the app look off-brand on
    // the theme most users see.
    final colors = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((t) => t.colors));
    final base = colors.softSurface;
    final highlight = colors.isDark
        ? colors.card
        : colors.background;

    return Shimmer.fromColors(
      baseColor: base,
      highlightColor: highlight,
      child: Container(
        width: width,
        height: height,
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: base,
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(borderRadius),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
```

### Step 3 — Adopt `AzResolveTransition` (grep-gated, at most three screens)

```bash
rg -n "SkeletonList\(|SkeletonBlock\(|AzSkeletonList\(" lib | head -20
rg -n "isLoading|loading" lib/screens/home_screen.dart | head -10
```

Pick **up to three** screens where a list is replaced by a skeleton (the highest-traffic ones). For
each, the change is mechanical:

1. Read the screen's existing boolean (whatever it uses for "first load").
2. Wrap each content block that has a skeleton twin:

```dart
        AzResolveTransition(
          phase: isLoadingFirstTime ? AzResolvePhase.loading : AzResolvePhase.resolved,
          index: 0,               // block 1 → 0, block 2 → 1, block 3 → 2 …
          skipEntrance: !isFirstVisitThisSession,
          announce: index == 0 && isFirstVisitThisSession,
          child: TheRealBlock(),
        ),
```

3. The skeleton itself stays where it is; `AzResolveTransition` only governs the **content's**
   arrival.

> **Rules that make this feel premium rather than busy:**
> - `index` must match the order the skeleton drew its blocks. The reveal order *is* the effect.
> - `skipEntrance: true` on every return to a screen the user already saw this session (the same
>   principle TASK-008 applies to Home's entrance).
> - `announce: true` at most once per screen, on index 0, and only where data genuinely arrived
>   (never on a screen that re-renders from a cached value).
> - Never exceed index 5: MotionTokens caps the delay at 300ms anyway, so more indices just make the
>   intent unclear.

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

Widget _host(Widget child, {bool reduce = false}) => MaterialApp(

void main() {

      phase: AzResolvePhase.loading,
      child: Text('block'),

    await tester.pumpWidget(_host(const AzResolveTransition(
      phase: AzResolvePhase.resolved,
      child: Text('block'),
    )));
    await tester.pumpAndSettle();

    expect(find.text('block'), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('a later index still lands (stagger is capped, not dropped)',
      (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(_host(const AzResolveTransition(
      phase: AzResolvePhase.resolved,
      index: 20,
      child: Text('block'),
    )));
    // 300ms cap + 350ms entrance + slack.
    await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 700));
    expect(tester.widget<Opacity>(find.byType(Opacity).first).opacity, 1.0);
  });
}

2. Return to that screen in the same session: content is simply there (no entrance).
3. Skeletons are now warm-white in light mode and near-black in dark mode — check both, and check the
   shimmer no longer reads as blue-grey.
4. Enable OS reduce-motion: content cross-fades in 180ms with **zero** movement and no stagger, and a
   haptic still fires once if `announce` was set.

### Do NOT

- Do **not** add `AzResolveTransition` around every widget on a screen. It is for the **skeleton

  cap is what stops a 20-row list from becoming an 800ms wait.

  post-frame callback in Step 1 exists solely for that reason.

## G.5 — TASK-024: Reduced motion as a designed state (`AzMotion`)

### Why

The app *respects* `MediaQuery.disableAnimations` in `MotionTokens.accessibleDuration` (verified,
L79-81) and in the nav — but "respecting" currently means "some things stop", decided per call site.
The assessment asks for the stronger, rarer thing (§8.6): a **designed** reduced-motion state where

- transitions become cross-fades at `MotionTokens.control` (180ms),
- staggers collapse to zero,
- parallax is disabled,
- and **informational motion survives** — a rate-direction colour flash still flashes, the sheen still
  communicates "premium surface" via a *static* gradient, but nothing travels.

Today there is no single place that can answer "may I move?" for a screen that isn't a token call
(e.g. a gesture-driven parallax). `TASK-026` added the user's own override. This task is the resolver
that reads both.

### Files — NEW

- `lib/theme/az_motion.dart`
- `test/theme/az_motion_test.dart`

### Files — MODIFY

- Nothing required. Adoption is a per-screen, grep-gated follow-up (Step 3). This is deliberate: a
  resolver that nothing is forced to use cannot break a build, and each adoption is trivially
  revertible.

### Pre-flight

```bash
rg -n "disableAnimations" lib | wc -l
# EXPECT: record it. These are the existing ad-hoc checks this task will eventually
#         replace one-by-one.

rg -n "AzMotion" lib | wc -l
# EXPECT: 0.

rg -n "accessibleDuration" lib | wc -l
# EXPECT: record it — Step 1's resolver DELEGATES to this, it does not replace it.
```

### Step 1 — NEW `lib/theme/az_motion.dart`

```dart
// lib/theme/az_motion.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ MOTION  (TASK-024)
//
// One question, one answer: "may I move, and how far may I go?"
//
//   AzMotion.of(context).travel         → false when motion must be skipped
//   AzMotion.duration(context, d)       → d, or Duration.zero when travel is off
//   AzMotion.informational(context, d)  → d, or MotionTokens.control when off
//   AzMotion.scale(context, amount)     → parallax/tilt amounts, zeroed when off
//
// Three inputs, in priority order:
//   1. The user's explicit override (TASK-026: 'Follow phone' / Always / Never)
//   2. The OS flag (MediaQuery.disableAnimations)
//   3. Defaults
//
// WHY THIS EXISTS: `MotionTokens.accessibleDuration` answers the OS question only,
// in a token call. A screen with gesture-driven parallax, a tilt sheen, or a
// physics-driven spring has no token to call — so it invented its own check, or
// forgot one. This is the single resolver for those cases, and it is the ONLY
// place that knows the difference between motion that must stop (travel) and
// motion that carries information (a colour flash, a state change).
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/sensory_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';

class AzMotion {
  /// True when spatial motion is permitted.
  final bool travel;

  const AzMotion._travel(this.travel);

  static AzMotion of(BuildContext context) {
    final osOff = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
    final reduce = AzSensory.reduceMotionOverrideIsSet
        ? AzSensory.reduceMotionOverride
        : osOff;
    return reduce ? const AzMotion._travel(false) : const AzMotion._travel(true);
  }

  /// Spatial motion: fades, slides, springs, staggers, parallax, tilt.
  /// Returns [Duration.zero] when motion is off — the caller's widget should then
  /// render its final state directly.
  static Duration duration(BuildContext context, Duration normal) =>
      of(context).travel ? normal : Duration.zero;

  /// Informational motion: a rate flashing its direction colour, a selection ring
  /// appearing, an error pulsing once. This is NEVER zeroed — the information is
  /// the point, it just stops travelling. It collapses to the control tempo.
  static Duration informational(BuildContext context, Duration normal) =>
      of(context).travel ? normal : MotionTokens.control;

  /// Stagger, with the cap applied by the token layer.
  static Duration stagger(BuildContext context, int index) =>
      of(context).travel ? MotionTokens.staggerDelay(index) : Duration.zero;

  /// A multiplier for parallax / tilt / perspective amounts (0.0 when off).
  static double scale(BuildContext context, double amount) =>
      of(context).travel ? amount : 0.0;

  /// Convenience for builders that need one switch.
  static T pick<T>(BuildContext context, {required T moving, required T still}) =>
      of(context).travel ? moving : still;
}
```

> Note the deliberate asymmetry: `duration` may return zero, but `informational` **never** does. That
> one line is the difference between "accessibility" and "accessibility done as craft" — a user who
> has reduced motion on still needs to know a rate moved against them.

### Step 2 — NEW `test/theme/az_motion_test.dart`

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/sensory_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/az_motion.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';

/// Borrows the winning pattern from the sub-agent reviews: resolve a Duration to
/// microseconds and compare, so a spring/curve residual can never be compared
/// against a float with `==`.
int _us(Duration d) => d.inMicroseconds;

void main() {
  tearDown(() => AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences()));

  testWidgets('OS flag off ⇒ travel allowed and durations pass through',
      (tester) async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences());
    Duration? seen;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: MediaQuery(
        data: const MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: false),
        child: Builder(builder: (context) {
          seen = AzMotion.duration(context, MotionTokens.emphasized);
          return const SizedBox();
        }),
      ),
    ));
    expect(_us(seen!), _us(MotionTokens.emphasized));
  });

  testWidgets('OS flag on ⇒ travel stops but information survives',
      (tester) async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences());
    Duration? spatial;
    Duration? info;
    double? parallax;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: MediaQuery(
        data: const MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: true),
        child: Builder(builder: (context) {
          spatial = AzMotion.duration(context, MotionTokens.emphasized);
          info = AzMotion.informational(context, MotionTokens.ambient);
          parallax = AzMotion.scale(context, 8.0);
          return const SizedBox();
        }),
      ),
    ));
    expect(_us(spatial!), 0);
    expect(_us(info!), _us(MotionTokens.control));
    expect(parallax, 0.0);
  });

  testWidgets('the user override beats the OS in both directions',
      (tester) async {
    // OS says move, user says stop.
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(forceReduceMotion: true));
    Duration? forcedStill;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: MediaQuery(
        data: const MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: false),
        child: Builder(builder: (context) {
          forcedStill = AzMotion.duration(context, MotionTokens.emphasized);
          return const SizedBox();
        }),
      ),
    ));
    expect(_us(forcedStill!), 0);

    // OS says stop, user says move.
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(forceReduceMotion: false));
    Duration? forcedMove;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: MediaQuery(
        data: const MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: true),
        child: Builder(builder: (context) {
          forcedMove = AzMotion.duration(context, MotionTokens.emphasized);
          return const SizedBox();
        }),
      ),
    ));
    expect(_us(forcedMove!), _us(MotionTokens.emphasized));
  });

  testWidgets('stagger respects the token cap in both modes', (tester) async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences());
    Duration? capped;
    Duration? zeroed;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: MediaQuery(
        data: const MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: false),
        child: Builder(builder: (context) {
          capped = AzMotion.stagger(context, 40);
          return const SizedBox();
        }),
      ),
    ));
    expect(_us(capped!), _us(MotionTokens.staggerMax));

    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: MediaQuery(
        data: const MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: true),
        child: Builder(builder: (context) {
          zeroed = AzMotion.stagger(context, 3);
          return const SizedBox();
        }),
      ),
    ));
    expect(_us(zeroed!), 0);
  });

  testWidgets('pick() chooses the designed still-state, not a blank', (tester) async {
    AzSensory.apply(const SensoryPreferences(forceReduceMotion: true));
    String? chosen;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: Builder(builder: (context) {
        chosen = AzMotion.pick(context, moving: 'slide', still: 'crossfade');
        return const SizedBox();
      }),
    ));
    expect(chosen, 'crossfade'); // not '' — there is always a designed still-state
  });
}
```

### Visual + behavioural acceptance

1. **Reduce motion → Never** (user override) while the OS flag is ON: the app moves fully again.
   This is the point — the user override is authoritative in **both** directions.
2. **Reduce motion → Always**: tab changes become 180ms cross-fades; nothing slides; the
   holographic surface keeps its gradient but stops responding to tilt.
3. With reduce-motion on, trigger a rate refresh (NEW-G once it ships): the rate **still** flashes its
   direction colour. Information is preserved; travel is not.
4. Accessibility scanner (TalkBack/VoiceOver) traversal is unaffected: no element becomes unreachable
   because motion was removed.

### Do NOT

- Do **not** delete or bypass `MotionTokens.accessibleDuration`. `AzMotion` delegates to the same
  concept; the existing API stays (A.3 rule 2).
- Do **not** use `AzMotion.duration` for informational motion. If the motion *is* the message, use
  `AzMotion.informational`. Choosing wrong here is how apps ship "reduced motion" that hides state
  changes from users who need them most.
- Do **not** sweep the 224 inline durations in this task. Adoption is the priority list, one screen at
  a time.

## G.6 — TASK-025: Accent identities + per-vertical accent (and F-001's stale comment)

### Why

`theme_provider.dart` L11-17 still advertises **"11 distinct visual identities"** and "Immersive
Planetary Themes" while the enum has two values (verified L19-27). The assessment's recommendation
(§8.7) is *not* to restore eleven themes — it is to ship **four accent identities** (Gold, Teal,
Indigo, Rose) that re-tint `accent` / `accentSecondary` / `accentSurface` / `glow` while the surface
ladder stays identical. Fewer themes, more expression. And §6.3 adds the second half: while the user
is inside a Marketplace vertical, that vertical's hue *becomes* the accent for the session.

This is the change that makes the app feel authored per-context rather than "one gold app".

### Files — MODIFY

- `lib/providers/theme_provider.dart` (one file — the accent model, the stale comment, and a
  single optional parameter on `getThemeData`).

### Files — NEW

- `test/theme/accent_identities_test.dart`

### Pre-flight

```bash
rg -n "11 distinct visual identities" lib/providers/theme_provider.dart   # EXPECT: 1 (L14)
rg -n "enum AzamanTheme" lib/providers/theme_provider.dart                # EXPECT: 1
rg -n "static ThemeData getThemeData" lib/providers/theme_provider.dart    # EXPECT: 1
rg -n "getThemeData\\(" lib | wc -l                                        # EXPECT: record it
rg -n "getColors\\(" lib | wc -l                                           # EXPECT: record it
rg -n "accentSecondary|colors.accent" lib | wc -l                          # EXPECT: thousands
```

> **The one rule that makes this safe:** `getColors` is **static** and is called directly from
> non-widget code. The accent must therefore be applied in the **instance** getters
> (`ThemeProvider.colors` / `.themeData`, verified L104-105) and in `getThemeData`'s optional
> parameter — never by changing what the static `getColors(theme)` returns. That way every existing
> static call site keeps working, and only the live app gets the accent.

### Step 2 — Add the accent model to `theme_provider.dart`

Insert directly after the `AzamanTheme` enum (after its closing brace at L27):

```dart
/// The four accent identities. Surfaces never change; only the accent family does.
enum AzAccent { gold, teal, indigo, rose }

/// One accent family in both brightnesses.
///
/// `onAccent` is part of the contract, not an afterthought: gold on white needs
/// dark ink, indigo on black needs white ink. Getting this wrong is how a "theme
/// picker" ships unreadable buttons.
class AzAccentFamily {
  final AzAccent id;
  final Color lightAccent;
  final Color lightOnAccent;
  final Color lightSecondary;
  final Color darkAccent;
  final Color darkOnAccent;
  final Color darkSecondary;

  const AzAccentFamily({
    required this.id,
    required this.lightAccent,
    required this.lightOnAccent,
    required this.lightSecondary,
    required this.darkAccent,
    required this.darkOnAccent,
    required this.darkSecondary,
  });

  Color accentFor(bool isDark) => isDark ? darkAccent : lightAccent;
  Color onAccentFor(bool isDark) => isDark ? darkOnAccent : lightOnAccent;
  Color secondaryFor(bool isDark) => isDark ? darkSecondary : lightSecondary;

  static const Map<AzAccent, AzAccentFamily> all = {
    // Gold is the current brand default — the light values match the existing
    // AzamanColors.accent / accentSecondary exactly, so choosing it changes
    // nothing visually. That is the point: the new default is the old app.
    AzAccent.gold: AzAccentFamily(
      id: AzAccent.gold,
      lightAccent: Color(0xFFB8860B),
      lightOnAccent: Colors.white,
      lightSecondary: Color(0xFF8B6914),
      darkAccent: Color(0xFFE0AE3A),
      darkOnAccent: Colors.black,
      darkSecondary: Color(0xFFF59E0B),
    ),
    AzAccent.teal: AzAccentFamily(
      id: AzAccent.teal,
      lightAccent: Color(0xFF0E7C7B),
      lightOnAccent: Colors.white,
      lightSecondary: Color(0xFF0F766E),
      darkAccent: Color(0xFF2DD4BF),
      darkOnAccent: Colors.black,
      darkSecondary: Color(0xFF5EEAD4),
    ),
    AzAccent.indigo: AzAccentFamily(
      id: AzAccent.indigo,
      lightAccent: Color(0xFF4338CA),
      lightOnAccent: Colors.white,
      lightSecondary: Color(0xFF3730A3),
      darkAccent: Color(0xFF8B9BFF),
      darkOnAccent: Colors.black,
      darkSecondary: Color(0xFFA5B4FC),
    ),
    AzAccent.rose: AzAccentFamily(
      id: AzAccent.rose,
      lightAccent: Color(0xFFBE123C),
      lightOnAccent: Colors.white,
      lightSecondary: Color(0xFF9F1239),
      darkAccent: Color(0xFFFB7185),
      darkOnAccent: Colors.black,
      darkSecondary: Color(0xFFFDA4AF),
    ),
  };
}
```

> Contrast note for the reviewer: every `lightAccent` above is ≥ 4.5:1 against white except
> `gold` (B8860B ≈ 3.6:1 against pure white), which is why **gold's `onAccent` is white but gold is
> only used for fills, rings, and icons ≥ 18px**, never for body text — and why `textPrimary` stays
> near-black. The test in Step 6 asserts the luminance ordering that keeps this true.

### Step 3 — `AzAccentFamily.withAccent` on `AzamanColors` (additive, no constructor change)

Inside the `AzamanColors` class (verified L271-326), insert **before** the closing brace, after the
existing alias getters:

```dart
  /// Ink for text/icons placed ON the accent. Derived, not stored, so no
  /// constructor changes and no call site changes: this matches the rule the
  /// framework bridge already uses (light theme → white ink, dark → black ink).
  Color get onAccent => isDark ? Colors.black : Colors.white;

  /// The same surface ladder, a different accent family. Surfaces, text and
  /// semantic colours are copied verbatim — only the accent family moves.
  ///
  /// `accentSurface` stays a low-alpha tint of the new accent so soft chips and
  /// selected rows re-tint with it; `glow` follows the accent because the glow
  /// is what makes a Level-5 surface feel lit by its own colour.
  AzamanColors withAccent(AzAccent accent) {
    final family = AzAccentFamily.all[accent] ?? AzAccentFamily.all[AzAccent.gold]!;
    final Color nextAccent = family.accentFor(isDark);
    return AzamanColors(
      isDark: isDark,
      name: '${name} · ${accent.name}',
      icon: icon,
      background: background,
      surface: surface,
      card: card,
      softSurface: softSurface,
      divider: divider,
      accent: nextAccent,
      accentSecondary: family.secondaryFor(isDark),
      accentSurface: nextAccent.withValues(alpha: 0.10),
      success: success,
      danger: danger,
      warning: warning,
      textPrimary: textPrimary,
      textSecondary: textSecondary,
      textTertiary: textTertiary,
      glow: nextAccent,
      scaffoldBackground: scaffoldBackground,
      border: border,
    );
  }
```

> This is the second half of the "two apps" fix from the assessment's §0. The Marketplace leaks

### Step 5 — NEW `lib/theme/az_vertical_accent.dart` (the second half of §6.3)

```dart
// lib/theme/az_vertical_accent.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ VERTICAL ACCENT  (TASK-025) — consumed by NEW-I's Marketplace worlds
//
// While the user is inside a Marketplace vertical, that vertical borrows the
// accent for the SESSION. Restaurants warm the app, Hotels cool it, Transit goes
// teal, Retail stays on the user's own identity.
//
// Session-only by design: the user's saved accent is never overwritten by
// browsing. Leaving the vertical restores it instantly, with no persistence and
// no "why is my app a different colour now" support ticket.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';

/// The borrowed accent for the current vertical, or null when outside one.
final verticalAccentProvider = StateProvider<AzAccent?>((ref) => null);

class AzVerticalAccentScope extends ConsumerWidget {
  final AzAccent accent;
  final Widget child;

  const AzVerticalAccentScope({
    super.key,
    required this.accent,
    required this.child,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    // Set on the first frame of the vertical and cleared on dispose, so no screen
    // has to remember to undo it.
    WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
      if (ref.read(verticalAccentProvider) != accent) {
        ref.read(verticalAccentProvider.notifier).state = accent;
      }
    });
    return child;
  }
}

/// The colours the app should use right now: the user's identity, overridden by
/// the vertical if one is active. Screens should read THIS at the shell level;
/// nothing inside a vertical reads it (they read `themeProvider.colors`, which
/// already reflects the resolution below).
final resolvedAzamanColorsProvider = Provider<AzamanColors>((ref) {
  final theme = ref.watch(themeProvider);
  final vertical = ref.watch(verticalAccentProvider);
  final base = ThemeProvider.getColors(theme.currentTheme);
  return base.withAccent(vertical ?? theme.accent);
});
```

Wire it once, in the shell: `AzamanApp.build` (in `main.dart`) already watches
`theme_pkg.themeProvider.select((t) => t.themeData)`. Change that line to:

```dart
    final vertical = ref.watch(verticalAccentProvider);
    final themeData = ref.watch(theme_pkg.themeProvider.select(
      (t) => ThemeProvider.getThemeData(t.currentTheme, accent: vertical ?? t.accent),
    ));
```

> This is a **provider-level** override rather than a `Theme` widget inside the vertical: it means the
> nav bar, the sheets and the system UI all move together. A vertical that only re-tints its own
> content is a theme in a box — and the whole point of §6.3 is that being in Restaurants *looks*
> different.

### Step 6 — The accent picker (memory of TASK-026's mount pattern)

Add **one** call site in the settings surface, as a sibling of `SensoryPreferencesSection()`:

```dart

```

…with this widget appended to `lib/widgets/sensory_preferences_section.dart`'s file (same file, so the
"Feel" group is one visual unit and no fourth settings file appears):

```dart
class AccentIdentityRow extends ConsumerWidget {
  const AccentIdentityRow({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    final colors = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((t) => t.colors));
    final current = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((t) => t.accent));

    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 12, 16, 16),
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text('Identity',
              style: TextStyle(
                color: colors.textPrimary,
                fontSize: 14.5,
                fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
              )),
          const SizedBox(height: 2),
          Text('Your accent, everywhere in Azaman',
              style: TextStyle(color: colors.textTertiary, fontSize: 12)),
          const SizedBox(height: 12),
          Row(
            children: [
              for (final a in AzAccent.values) ...[
                GestureDetector(
                  behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
                  onTap: () {
                    ref.read(themeProvider).setAccent(a);
                    AzamanHaptics.selection();
                  },
                  child: Container(
                    width: 40,
                    height: 40,
                    decoration: BoxDecoration(
                      shape: BoxShape.circle,
                      color: AzAccentFamily.all[a]!.accentFor(colors.isDark),
                      border: Border.all(
                        color: current == a ? colors.textPrimary : colors.border,
                        width: current == a ? 2.5 : 0.5,
                      ),
                    ),
                  ),
                ),
                const SizedBox(width: 12),
              ],
            ],
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

> Deliberately **not** a list with labels. A row of four colour discs is understood instantly, needs no
> reading, and is the same interaction language as the swatch row TASK-012 ships for product variants.
> Consistency across surfaces is what makes an app feel designed rather than assembled.

void main() {

    expect(goldDark.accent, AzAccentFamily.all[AzAccent.gold]!.darkAccent);

      expect(themed.softSurface, base.softSurface);
      expect(themed.divider, base.divider);
      expect(themed.textPrimary, base.textPrimary);
      expect(themed.textSecondary, base.textSecondary);
      expect(themed.textTertiary, base.textTertiary);
      expect(themed.success, base.success);
      expect(themed.danger, base.danger);
      expect(themed.warning, base.warning);
      expect(themed.border, base.border);
      expect(themed.scaffoldBackground, base.scaffoldBackground);
      expect(themed.isDark, base.isDark);
      // …and the accent family DID move
      expect(themed.accent, AzAccentFamily.all[a]!.accentFor(false));
      expect(themed.glow, themed.accent);
    }
  });

  test('onAccent is legible on its own accent (>= 3:1 for graphics)', () {
    double ratio(Color a, Color b) {
      final la = a.computeLuminance();
      final lb = b.computeLuminance();
      final hi = la > lb ? la : lb;
      final lo = la > lb ? lb : la;
      return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05);
    }

    for (final isDark in [true, false]) {
      for (final a in AzAccent.values) {
        final c = ThemeProvider.getColors(
                isDark ? AzamanTheme.dark : AzamanTheme.light)
            .withAccent(a);

            reason: 'onAccent must be readable on ${a.name} (isDark=$isDark)');
        expect(ratio(c.textPrimary, c.background), greaterThan(4.5),
            reason: 'textPrimary must stay AA on the page for ${a.name}');

        expect(cs.primaryContainer, isNotNull);
        expect(cs.outlineVariant, isNotNull);
        expect(cs.primary, ThemeProvider.getColors(theme).withAccent(a).accent);
      }
    }
  });

  test('the default getThemeData call still works (TASK-004 guard)', () {
    final td = ThemeProvider.getThemeData(AzamanTheme.light);
    expect(td.brightness, Brightness.light);
  });
}

## G.7 — NEW-K: One image path, one avatar (and the last lavender leak in a core widget)

### Why

The assessment (§10.8, §10.9) asks for one avatar widget and one image widget. The verified source
makes this worse than "inconsistency" — it is a **colour-system leak inside a core widget**:

- `lib/widgets/azaman_network_image.dart` — the very widget the assessment recommends as *the* image
  path — reads `Theme.of(context).colorScheme.surfaceContainerHighest` (L79-83) and
  `colorScheme.onSurface` (L88-96) for its placeholder and fallback. So the recommended single image
  path renders M3-baseline lavender whenever it fails to load — in the Marketplace, in chat, in retail
  grids. **The fix must happen before any migration to it**, or the migration spreads the leak.
- `lib/widgets/chat_avatar.dart` (verified) already does initials + a hashed gradient + a presence dot
  + a hero flight shuttle + reduced-motion awareness (L29-37, L103-105). It is genuinely good. It is
  missing three things the app needs everywhere: a **story-ring slot**, a **size-independent stroke**,
  and a **squircle/round switch** (ListTile wants a circle; the chat header wants the squircle).

So NEW-K is: fix the image widget's colours, then promote the avatar into `AzAvatar` as the additive
superset of `ChatAvatar` (keeping `ChatAvatar` as a deprecated-but-working alias so its call sites
don't change — A.3 rule 2).

### Files — MODIFY

- `lib/widgets/azaman_network_image.dart` (the colour fix — Step 1)
- `lib/widgets/chat_avatar.dart` (add the story-ring slot + shape switch — Step 2)

### Files — NEW

- `lib/widgets/az_avatar.dart` (the canonical name, delegating to `ChatAvatar`)

### Step 1 — `azaman_network_image.dart`: use `AzamanColors`

Replace the class declaration and the two colour helpers (currently L13-98):

```dart
class AzamanNetworkImage extends ConsumerWidget {
  final String? imageUrl;
  final double? width;
  final double? height;
  final BoxFit fit;
  final BorderRadius? borderRadius;

  /// Optional drawable placeholder. Defaults to a themed block; pass
  /// `SkeletonBlock` when the parent is a list that will resolve (TASK-022).
  final Widget Function(BuildContext, String)? placeholder;
  final Widget Function(BuildContext, String, Object)? errorWidget;

  const AzamanNetworkImage({
    super.key,
    required this.imageUrl,
    this.width,
    this.height,
    this.fit = BoxFit.cover,
    this.borderRadius,
    this.placeholder,
    this.errorWidget,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    final colors = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((t) => t.colors));
    if (width != null && height != null) {
      return _buildImage(context, colors, width!, height!);
    }
    return LayoutBuilder(
      builder: (context, constraints) {
        final w = width ?? constraints.maxWidth;
        final h = height ?? constraints.maxHeight;
        final resolvedW = w.isFinite ? w : 400.0;
        final resolvedH = h.isFinite ? h : 400.0;
        return _buildImage(context, colors, resolvedW, resolvedH);
      },
    );
  }

  Widget _buildImage(
      BuildContext context, AzamanColors colors, double w, double h) {
    final dpr = MediaQuery.devicePixelRatioOf(context);
    final targetW = (w * dpr).round();
    final targetH = (h * dpr).round();

    Widget image;
    if (imageUrl == null || imageUrl!.isEmpty) {
      image = _fallback(colors, w, h);
    } else {
      image = CachedNetworkImage(
        imageUrl: imageUrl!,
        width: width,
        height: height,
        fit: fit,
        memCacheWidth: targetW,
        memCacheHeight: targetH,
        fadeInDuration: MotionTokens.control,
        placeholder: placeholder ?? (_, __) => _shimmerBlock(colors, w, h),
        errorWidget: errorWidget ?? (_, __, ___) => _fallback(colors, w, h),
      );
    }

    return borderRadius != null
        ? ClipRRect(borderRadius: borderRadius!, child: image)
        : image;
  }

  /// Deliberately a THEMED block, not M3 lavender. This widget is the app's
  /// single image path, so a leak here leaks everywhere.
  Widget _shimmerBlock(AzamanColors colors, double w, double h) => Container(
        width: width ?? w,
        height: height ?? h,
        color: colors.softSurface,
      );

  Widget _fallback(AzamanColors colors, double w, double h) => Container(
        width: width ?? w,
        height: height ?? h,
        color: colors.softSurface,
        child: Icon(
          Icons.image_outlined,
          size: (w * 0.35).clamp(16.0, 48.0),
          color: colors.textTertiary,
        ),
      );
}
```

import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';
```

> `ConsumerWidget` means no call site changes. `fadeInDuration: MotionTokens.control` replaces the
> hardcoded 200ms — one more inline duration folded into the token system.

// lib/widgets/az_avatar.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ AVATAR  (NEW-K)
//
// The one avatar widget. It is a thin, named alias of ChatAvatar so the app can
// migrate to a single import without a risky rename of a widget with many call
// sites (A.3 rules 1-2). When the last ChatAvatar call site is migrated, the old
// name can be deleted in its own tiny task — but the behaviour is identical
// today, so migrating is zero-risk and can happen one screen at a time.
// =============================================================================

export 'package:azaman/widgets/chat_avatar.dart' show ChatAvatar;

typedef AzAvatar = ChatAvatar;
```

> Using `typedef` + `export` means `AzAvatar(...)` is literally `ChatAvatar(...)`: identical

```dart
// lib/widgets/home/az_greeting_brain.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ GREETING BRAIN  (NEW-D)
//
// Home's top 60px stops being a string and becomes the app's VOICE.
//
// Priority order (highest first). Money events always beat pleasantries, because
// a user who just got paid does not want "Good morning":
//
//   1. moneyArrivedToday       → "Your GH₵ 400 cleared"
//   2. escrowReleasingInHours  → "Escrow releases in 3h"
//   3. susuDueTomorrow         → "Susu due tomorrow"
//   4. depositAwaitingApproval → "Waiting on your mobile-money approval"
//   5. streak ≥ 7              → "7-day streak"
//   6. time of day             → "Good morning" / "afternoon" / "evening"
//
// HONESTY RULES (F.5 / NEW-T): every input is nullable and NOTHING is invented.
// An unknown value skips its line. No fake streak, no invented payday, and no
// greeting that names an amount the app cannot verify.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

enum AzGreetingTone { neutral, positive, attention, warming }

class AzGreetingLine {
  final String text;

  /// Drives the glyph, and (only when [announceable]) a single quiet haptic.
  final AzGreetingTone tone;

  /// True only for a REAL event that just happened — the only case that may
  /// announce itself with a haptic or a sound (TASK-020's pairing rule).
  final bool announceable;

  const AzGreetingLine({
    required this.text,
    this.tone = AzGreetingTone.neutral,
    this.announceable = false,
  });
}

class AzGreetingInputs {
  final String? username;
  final DateTime now;

  /// A settled inflow today, already formatted by `AzMoney` (TASK-009a).
  final String? moneyArrivedToday;

  /// Hours until the next escrow release (null when none / unknown).
  final int? escrowReleasingInHours;

  final bool susuDueTomorrow;

  /// A deposit that is accepted-but-not-settled (NEW-P's `pending` state).
  final bool depositAwaitingApproval;

  /// Consecutive days with a real completed action. Null when unknown.
  final int? streakDays;

  const AzGreetingInputs({
    required this.now,
    this.username,
    this.moneyArrivedToday,
    this.escrowReleasingInHours,
    this.susuDueTomorrow = false,
    this.depositAwaitingApproval = false,
    this.streakDays,
  });
}

abstract class AzGreetingBrain {
  static AzGreetingLine resolve(AzGreetingInputs i) {
    if (i.moneyArrivedToday != null && i.moneyArrivedToday!.isNotEmpty) {
      return AzGreetingLine(
        text: 'Your ${i.moneyArrivedToday} cleared',
        tone: AzGreetingTone.positive,
        announceable: true,
      );
    }
    final hours = i.escrowReleasingInHours;
    if (hours != null && hours >= 0) {
      return AzGreetingLine(
        text: hours == 0
            ? 'Escrow releases now'
            : 'Escrow releases in ${_hours(hours)}',
        tone: AzGreetingTone.attention,
      );
    }
    if (i.susuDueTomorrow) {
      return const AzGreetingLine(
          text: 'Susu due tomorrow', tone: AzGreetingTone.attention);
    }
    if (i.depositAwaitingApproval) {
      return const AzGreetingLine(
        text: 'Waiting on your mobile-money approval',
        tone: AzGreetingTone.attention,
      );
    }
    final streak = i.streakDays;
    if (streak != null && streak >= 7) {
      return AzGreetingLine(
        text: '$streak-day streak',
        tone: AzGreetingTone.warming,
      );
    }
    return AzGreetingLine(
      text: '${_partOfDay(i.now)}, ${_name(i.username)}',
      tone: AzGreetingTone.neutral,
    );
  }

  /// "in 3h" / "in under an hour" — never "in 0h", never a negative duration.
  static String _hours(int h) {
    if (h < 1) return 'under an hour';
    if (h == 1) return '1h';
    return '${h}h';
  }

  static String _partOfDay(DateTime now) {
    final h = now.hour;
    if (h < 12) return 'Good morning';
    if (h < 17) return 'Good afternoon';
    return 'Good evening';
  }

  static String _name(String? username) {
    final n = (username ?? '').trim();
    if (n.isEmpty) return 'there'; // never a dangling comma, never "null"
    // First name only: "Good morning, Kwame" reads like a person; a full legal
    // name reads like a bank statement.
    return n.split(RegExp(r'\s+')).first;
  }

  /// Which glyph the header shows. Kept here so the widget stays dumb.
  static IconData glyphFor(AzGreetingTone tone) {
    switch (tone) {
      case AzGreetingTone.positive:
        return Icons.trending_up_rounded;
      case AzGreetingTone.attention:
        return Icons.schedule_rounded;
      case AzGreetingTone.warming:
        return Icons.local_fire_department_outlined;
      case AzGreetingTone.neutral:
        return Icons.wb_sunny_outlined;
    }
  }
}
```

### Step 2 — Mount the brain in `_GreetingTitle` (post-TASK-008)

`_GreetingTitle` (verified L303) currently renders a static string. Replace its text source with the
brain and add the glyph:

```dart

    // absent value means the brain skips that line rather than inventing one.
    final user = ref.watch(authProvider).user;
    final summary = ref.watch(homeSummaryProvider);
    final now = DateTime.now();

    final line = AzGreetingBrain.resolve(AzGreetingInputs(
      now: now,
      username: user?.name,
      // Only a SETTLED inflow qualifies (NEW-P's `confirmed` state).
      moneyArrivedToday: summary.moneyArrivedTodayFormatted,
      escrowReleasingInHours: summary.nextEscrowReleaseHours,
      susuDueTomorrow: summary.susuDueTomorrow,
      depositAwaitingApproval: summary.depositAwaitingApproval,

```

Then render `line.text` where the greeting string was, prefixed by the glyph:

```dart
        Row(
          children: [
            AnimatedSwitcher(
              duration: MotionTokens.control,
              child: Icon(
                AzGreetingBrain.glyphFor(line.tone),
                key: ValueKey(line.tone),
                size: 20,
                color: colors.accent,
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(width: 8),
            Expanded(
              child: AnimatedSwitcher(
                duration: MotionTokens.standard,
                transitionBuilder: (child, anim) =>
                    FadeTransition(opacity: anim, child: child),
                child: Text(

                  key: ValueKey(line.text),

```

> **The `AnimatedSwitcher` is not decoration.** The greeting can change while the user is looking at
> Home (a trade settles, an escrow releases). Cross-fading the words — instead of swapping them — is
> what makes the app feel like it *noticed*. It uses `MotionTokens.standard` (220ms), not
> `emphasized`: this is a label, not a scene.

> **What these `summary.*` fields are.** `homeSummaryProvider` already exists (it drives
> `today_widget.dart`, verified import at L25). Add the four nullable fields it lacks
> (`moneyArrivedTodayFormatted`, `nextEscrowReleaseHours`, `susuDueTomorrow`,
> `depositAwaitingApproval`, `streakDays`) to that notifier, sourced from providers that already hold
> the truth. If a field cannot be sourced, leave it **null** — that is the whole point.

### Step 3 — NEW `lib/widgets/home/az_insight_card.dart`

One insight, one number, seven bars. Renders **nothing** when the data is not verifiable (F.5).

```dart
// lib/widgets/home/az_insight_card.dart
// =============================================================================
// AZ INSIGHT CARD  (NEW-D)
//
// "You spent GH₵ 240 on food this week — 18% less than last." This is the
// difference between a wallet and a financial companion (assessment §3.3). It is
// also the easiest place in the app to LIE, so the contract is:
//
//   * No data → render SizedBox.shrink(). Never a placeholder statistic.
//   * The comparison is shown only when BOTH periods exist.
//   * The sentence is written FOR the direction of the change.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';

import 'package:azaman/providers/theme_provider.dart';
import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';

class AzInsightCard extends ConsumerWidget {
  /// Already-formatted amount from `AzMoney` (TASK-009a).
  final String? amountText;
  final String? category;

  /// Fractional change vs the previous period. Negative = spent less.
  final double? changeFraction;

  /// Up to 7 daily values for the sparkline (oldest first).
  final List<double>? sparkline;

  final VoidCallback? onTap;

  const AzInsightCard({
    super.key,
    this.amountText,
    this.category,
    this.changeFraction,
    this.sparkline,
    this.onTap,
  });

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    // The honesty gate: without an amount and a category there is no insight.
    if (amountText == null || category == null) return const SizedBox.shrink();

    final colors = ref.watch(themeProvider.select((t) => t.colors));
    final change = changeFraction;
    final less = change != null && change < 0;
    final deltaColor = change == null
        ? colors.textTertiary
        : (less ? colors.success : colors.warning);

    return GestureDetector(
      behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
      onTap: onTap,
      child: Container(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        decoration: BoxDecoration(
          color: colors.card,
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          border: Border.all(color: colors.border, width: 0.5),
        ),
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Row(
              children: [
                Text('This week',
                    style: TextStyle(
                      color: colors.textTertiary,
                      fontSize: 11.5,
                      fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
                      letterSpacing: 0.4,
                    )),
                const Spacer(),
                if (change != null)
                  Text(
                    '${less ? '▼' : '▲'} ${(change.abs() * 100).round()}%',
                    style: TextStyle(
                      color: deltaColor,
                      fontSize: 12,
                      fontWeight: FontWeight.w700,
                    ),
                  ),
              ],
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 8),
            Text(
              '$amountText on $category',
              style: TextStyle(
                color: colors.textPrimary,
                fontSize: 17,
                fontWeight: FontWeight.w700,
                height: 1.25,
              ),
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 4),
            Text(
              change == null
                  ? 'Not enough history yet to compare.'
                  : (less
                      ? 'Less than last week. Whatever you changed, keep it.'
                      : 'More than last week.'),
              style: TextStyle(
                  color: colors.textTertiary, fontSize: 12, height: 1.4),
            ),
            if (sparkline != null && sparkline!.length >= 2) ...[
              const SizedBox(height: 14),
              SizedBox(
                height: 26,
                child: Row(
                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end,
                  children: [
                    for (var i = 0; i < sparkline!.length; i++)
                      Expanded(
                        child: Padding(
                          padding: const EdgeInsets.only(right: 3),
                          child: AnimatedContainer(
                            duration: MotionTokens.standard,
                            curve: MotionTokens.enter,
                            height: 6 + (20 * _norm(sparkline!, i)),
                            decoration: BoxDecoration(
                              color: colors.accent.withValues(
                                  alpha:
                                      i == sparkline!.length - 1 ? 1.0 : 0.35),
                              borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(2),
                            ),
                          ),
                        ),
                      ),
                  ],
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }

  /// Normalises bar [i] against the series max, with a floor so an all-zero week
  /// renders flat bars instead of dividing by zero.
  static double _norm(List<double> values, int i) {
    final max = values.reduce((a, b) => a > b ? a : b);
    if (max <= 0) return 0;
    return (values[i] / max).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  }
}
```

Mount it as the second card in the TASK-008 deck (`_BalanceCardsScroll`), passing
`insight?.amountText`, `insight?.category`, `insight?.changeFraction`, `insight?.daily`, and an
`onTap` that pushes `SpendingInsightsScreen`.

> Because the card collapses to `SizedBox.shrink()`, a user with no spending history sees the deck
> exactly as TASK-008 shipped it. Nothing is faked to fill the slot.

### Step 4 — the pull-to-refresh reward (NEW-D's third signal)

The refresh gesture already exists (`az_pull_to_refresh.dart` → `AzLogoRefreshIndicator`, 565
lines, real layout-space indicator, already honours `MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf`). **Do not
rewrite it.** This step only adds the two things it lacks: the semantic haptic and a tick-up
acknowledgement, both gated by TASK-026.

The indicator's own `onRefresh` is the seam. Pass a wrapped callback at the Home call site; do not
edit `az_logo_refresh_indicator.dart` and do not change `AzPullToRefresh`'s public constructor.

```dart
// at the Home call site (lib/screens/home_screen.dart, the AzPullToRefresh mount)
onRefresh: () async {
  final before = ref.read(hologramProvider).balance;      // whatever Home already reads
  await ref.read(homeSummaryProvider.notifier).refresh();
  // One threshold click when the user commits the pull — not a tick per pixel.
  // TASK-006 ships this name; if the probe below is empty, run TASK-006 first.
  AzamanHaptics.threshold();
  final after = ref.read(hologramProvider).balance;
  if (after > before) {
    // A settlement landed while refreshing. The money moving up on screen is
    // the reward; the haptic is the receipt.
    AzamanHaptics.moneyLanded();
  }
},
```

If the balance source is not readable synchronously at that point, drop the comparison and keep
`AzamanHaptics.threshold()` only. **Never fabricate a number to animate here** (F.5).

### Step 5 — action pills 4 → 3

The four pills are at `home_screen.dart` L346-355. Withdraw and History are two surfaces of the
same question ("what happened to my money?"), and four equal pills at 360dp is the layout
equivalent of a menu nobody chooses from.

Replace the `pills` list with three entries, folding Withdraw into a History surface that offers
both:

```dart
    final pills = [
      _PillData(label: "Add Money", icon: Icons.add,
        onTap: () => pushWithVerticalTransition(context, const DepositScreen(initialTab: DepositTab.fiat))),
      _PillData(label: "Send", icon: Icons.send_outlined,
        onTap: () => pushWithVerticalTransition(context, const SendMoneyScreen())),
      // One pill, two destinations. The sheet is the same Panel grammar NEW-B
      // standardises later; until then it is a plain modal sheet.
      _PillData(label: "History", icon: Icons.history,
        onTap: () => showModalBottomSheet<void>(
          context: context,
          backgroundColor: colors.surface,
          shape: const RoundedRectangleBorder(
            borderRadius: BorderRadius.vertical(top: Radius.circular(24)),
          ),
          builder: (_) => SafeArea(
            child: Column(
              mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
              children: [
                ListTile(
                  leading: const Icon(Icons.history),
                  title: const Text('Transaction history'),
                  onTap: () {
                    Navigator.of(context).pop();
                    pushWithVerticalTransition(context, const TransactionHistoryScreen());
                  },
                ),
                ListTile(
                  leading: const Icon(Icons.account_balance_outlined),
                  title: const Text('Withdraw'),
                  onTap: () {
                    Navigator.of(context).pop();
                    pushWithVerticalTransition(context, const WithdrawalScreen());
                  },
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        )),
    ];
```

> **Withdrawing is now two taps deep.** That is a real cost, and it is the right trade: withdrawal
> is a rare, considered action, and the review step it gains in NEW-P costs a tap anyway. If NEW-P
> has already landed, `WithdrawalScreen` opens on its own review stage, so the second tap buys real
> information. Confirm this reads correctly before shipping; do not ship a two-tap path to a
> one-tap screen.

## H.4 Accessibility is worse than NEW-R assumes — the real number is 3

NEW-R scopes an audit of "existing" controls. The measurement makes the scope concrete and larger

| `showDialog` sites | 37 |

Three `Semantics` call sites across 440 Dart files is not a partially-accessible app; it is an app
with **no accessibility layer at all**. NEW-R's ten-file list is therefore a floor, not a
complete inventory, and its framing ("newly authored widgets having Semantics is not a
remediation pass") understates the gap.

**Re-scope NEW-R before it is specced.** Its honest first step is a *sweep*, not an edit: an
inventory pass that lists every tappable icon-only control with its file and line, so the fix list

## H.5 Timer and lifecycle debt is bounded and findable

NEW-S (performance/lifecycle) is specified as a principle: "pause or dispose work when
offstage/hidden". It can be sharpened into a concrete first pass:

  step.

Do not let NEW-S expand beyond these two into a general performance project. The measurement says
the problem is 14 files, not "the app".

## H.6 What is genuinely missing from the entire brief: a visual regression system

This is the most valuable gap in the programme, and no part of the brief proposes it.

The repo has exactly **3 golden PNGs**, all in one folder, all for one shader. Every other premium
claim in Parts B–H — the glass lighting recipe (TASK-005), the holographic card (TASK-009c/009d),
the nav pill compression (TASK-010), the deck rail (TASK-008), the liquid backdrop, the receipt
artefact (TASK-021) — is a **visual** claim verified only by a human running the app and looking.

That is why this programme keeps stalling: the DoD in A.7 is "analyzer + build + the task's own
tests", and none of those can see a pixel. Every task's "Visual acceptance" section is
un-automatable, and humans are inconsistent reviewers of "does this feel premium".

- Rule: every golden test must disable animations deterministically (TASK-026's reduced-motion
  override, inside `MaterialApp.home`) and pin the surface size and pixel ratio, or it will be
  flaky on someone else's machine and get deleted within a week.
- Why this outranks more polish: it converts "premium" from an opinion into a diff. It is also the
  only mechanism that will let later parts of this brief be executed by someone other than the
  person who wrote them.

## G.9 — TASK-019: Today strip + ambient mode

### Why

§9.5/§9.6 ship two things on the same surface and therefore belong in one task. The Today strip is the
app's only *live* row: three chips that answer "what needs me right now" without a scroll. The ambient
mode is the temptation. §H.7 is explicit that idle beauty after 8s is retention engineering, not craft
— so this task specs the strip in full and **deliberately re-scopes ambient mode down to something
with a purpose**, or nothing at all.

**The decision this task makes explicit:** ambient mode is a real "today" summary that is *already on
screen*, not a new animation that appears when the user stops touching the phone. It dims secondary
chrome so the one row that matters reads first. It never plays sound, never fires a haptic, and never
re-animates on a timer. Idle motion that asks for attention the user did not give is what §H.7's
standing rule forbids.

**Dependency note:** anchors to post-TASK-008 Home. `_GreetingTitle` (L303), `_ActionPills` (L340),
`_BalanceCardsScroll` (L422), `_SusuShortcutCard` (L571) must still exist. `_NewWalletCard` is deleted
by TASK-008, so never reference it.

### Files — NEW

- `lib/widgets/home/az_today_strip.dart` (the model + the widget)
- `test/home/az_today_strip_test.dart`

### Files — MODIFY

- `lib/screens/home_screen.dart` — mount the strip above `_ActionPills`.
