### Step 1 — NEW `lib/widgets/home/az_today_strip.dart`

```dart
// lib/widgets/home/az_today_strip.dart
// =============================================================================
// TASK-019 — The Today strip: three live chips, and nothing else.
//
// The strip answers one question without a scroll: "what needs me right now?"
// Three chip kinds, ranked, and never more than three:
//
//   1. transitPass   — a boarding pass in the next 6h      (has a deadline)
//   2. delivery      — an order in transit                (has a deadline)
//   3. dueToday      — a Susu collection due today       (has a deadline)
//
// Every chip that renders has a real clock behind it. A chip with no deadline
// is a notification, and a notification on Home is noise, so there is no
// "general" chip kind and no way to add one without a deadline field.
//
// Ambient mode (Step 3) is NOT here, and its absence is deliberate: see
// §H.7. Idle motion that does not serve a glanceable purpose is retention
// engineering. This file ships the strip; the strip is the whole feature.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';

import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';
import 'package:azaman/utils/azaman_haptics.dart';
import 'package:azaman/widgets/premium_glass_container.dart';

/// The three things Home will ever ask about. Adding a fourth is a design
/// decision, not a code change: the strip is three chips because three fits
/// above the fold at 360dp without scrolling or truncating.
enum AzTodayKind { transitPass, delivery, dueToday }

/// What a chip renders. [deadline] is required, not optional — a chip without a
/// deadline has no honest reason to occupy prime screen space, and making it
/// optional would guarantee that someone eventually ships one.
@immutable
class AzTodayItem {
  const AzTodayItem({
    required this.kind,
    required this.title,
    required this.detail,
    required this.deadline,
    this.icon,
    this.onTap,
  });

  final AzTodayKind kind;
  final String title;

  /// One line, already shortened. The chip is ~180dp wide; the widget truncates
  /// with an ellipsis and the source should not rely on it.
  final String detail;

  /// Absolute instant. The chip's live countdown is computed from this, so a
  /// chip never shows a stale "in 5 min" that the user has to mentally correct.
  final DateTime deadline;

  /// Overrides the per-kind default glyph. Nullable because two chips of the
  /// same kind (two open orders) should still be distinguishable.
  final IconData? icon;

  /// User-initiated navigation. Null means "informational only" — the chip is
  /// still rendered, and tapping it is a no-op, because some facts (a Susu
  /// collection due) are worth knowing about without an action attached.
  final VoidCallback? onTap;
}

/// Rank order. Transit beats delivery beats due-today because a boarding window
/// that closes is the only irreversible consequence here; everything else stays
/// actionable for hours afterwards.
const Map<AzTodayKind, int> _kRank = {
  AzTodayKind.transitPass: 0,
  AzTodayKind.delivery: 1,
  AzTodayKind.dueToday: 2,
};

IconData _defaultIcon(AzTodayKind kind) => switch (kind) {
      AzTodayKind.transitPass => Icons.confirmation_number_outlined,
      AzTodayKind.delivery => Icons.local_shipping_outlined,
      AzTodayKind.dueToday => Icons.savings_outlined,
    };

/// Live time remaining, bucketed so the chip text stops jittering every second.
///
/// This is the single most important detail in the file. Rendering
/// `in 4m 59s` and rebuilding on a timer produces a row that mutates once per
/// second, which (a) makes the countdown unreadable and (b) means Home never
/// holds still. Bucketing to whole minutes below an hour and to hours below a
/// day means the label changes at most a handful of times over the life of a
/// chip, and the meaning is unchanged.
String azTodayRemainingLabel(DateTime now, DateTime deadline) {
  final remaining = deadline.difference(now);

  // Overdue reads as a fact, never as an alarm. No red, no exclamation, no
  // caps — §H.7's rule is that tone must never become a judgement, and "your
  // train left" is a neutral event.
  if (remaining.isNegative) return 'Passed';
  if (remaining.inMinutes < 1) return 'Now';

  if (remaining.inMinutes < 60) return 'in ${remaining.inMinutes} min';
  if (remaining.inHours < 24) {
    final h = remaining.inHours;
    return 'in $h ${h == 1 ? 'hr' : 'hrs'}';
  }
  final d = remaining.inDays;
  return 'in $d ${d == 1 ? 'day' : 'days'}';
}

/// The ranked, capped, empty-aware list the widget renders. Pure and
/// widget-free so it can be tested without pumping anything.
List<AzTodayItem> azTodayRank({required List<AzTodayItem> items}) {
  final sorted = [...items]
    ..sort((a, b) => _kRank[a.kind]!.compareTo(_kRank[b.kind]!));
  return sorted.take(3).toList(growable: false);
}

/// The strip itself.
///
/// Renders **nothing at all** when there is no data. An empty bordered row with
/// a shrug icon is worse than its absence: it spends the most valuable 48dp on
/// screen to say nothing, and it makes the chips above and below it look like
/// a permanent feature with a hole in it.
class AzTodayStrip extends ConsumerWidget {
  const AzTodayStrip({super.key, required this.items, this.now});

  final List<AzTodayItem> items;

  /// Injectable clock. Production omits it and gets `DateTime.now()`; tests pin
  /// it so countdown text is deterministic and never flakes at a minute
  /// boundary.
  final DateTime? now;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context, WidgetRef ref) {
    final ranked = azTodayRank(items: items);
    if (ranked.isEmpty) return const SizedBox.shrink();

    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 0, 16, 14),
      child: Row(
        children: [
          for (var i = 0; i < ranked.length; i++) ...[
            if (i > 0) const SizedBox(width: 8),
            Expanded(child: _Chip(item: ranked[i], now: now)),
          ],
        ],
      ),
    );
  }
}

class _Chip extends StatelessWidget {
  const _Chip({required this.item, required this.now});

  final AzTodayItem item;
  final DateTime? now;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = Theme.of(context);
    final colors = theme.colorScheme;
    final when = now ?? DateTime.now();

    final chip = Container(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 10, vertical: 9),
      decoration: BoxDecoration(
        color: colors.surfaceContainerHighest.withValues(alpha: 0.72),
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(14),
        border: Border.all(
          color: colors.outlineVariant.withValues(alpha: 0.5),
        ),
      ),
      child: Column(
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        children: [
          Row(
            children: [
              Icon(
                item.icon ?? _defaultIcon(item.kind),
                size: 14,
                color: colors.primary,
              ),
              const SizedBox(width: 5),
              Expanded(
                child: Text(
                  item.title,
                  maxLines: 1,
                  overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
                  style: theme.textTheme.labelSmall?.copyWith(
                    color: colors.onSurface,
                    fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
                  ),
                ),
              ),
            ],
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 3),
          Text(
            item.detail,
            maxLines: 1,
            overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
            style: theme.textTheme.bodySmall?.copyWith(
              color: colors.onSurfaceVariant,
            ),
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 2),
          Text(
            azTodayRemainingLabel(when, item.deadline),
            maxLines: 1,
            style: theme.textTheme.labelSmall?.copyWith(
              color: colors.primary,
              fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
            ),
          ),
        ],
      ),
    );

    // One haptic, on the user's tap, confirming the navigation — the pattern
    // TASK-010 established for the nav. Never on a timer, never on mount.
    if (item.onTap == null) return chip;

    return Semantics(
      button: true,
      label: '${item.title}. ${item.detail}. '
          '${azTodayRemainingLabel(when, item.deadline)}',
      child: GestureDetector(
        behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
        onTap: () {
          AzamanHaptics.nav();
          item.onTap!();
        },
        child: chip,
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

**`PremiumGlassContainer` is imported but deliberately unused in Step 1.** The strip sits on Home's
existing substrate; a new glass layer over the balance cards is a visual decision that belongs with
TASK-008's deck, not smuggled in here. Remove the import at adoption time if it stays unused —
`flutter analyze` will flag it.

### Step 2 — Mount the strip in `home_screen.dart`

Insert immediately **above** the `_ActionPills` child in the deck, so the reading order is
greeting → today's obligations → what you can do → what you own.

```dart
// Ranking happens inside AzTodayStrip; the call site just supplies the data.
// When there is no active order, trip or due collection, `items` is empty and
// the strip renders SizedBox.shrink() — no empty row.
AzTodayStrip(
  items: [
    if (activeTrip != null)
      AzTodayItem(
        kind: AzTodayKind.transitPass,
        title: activeTrip!.routeLabel,
        detail: activeTrip!.destinationLabel,
        deadline: activeTrip!.departureAt,
        onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).push(
          MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => activeTrip!.boardingScreen()),
        ),
      ),
    if (activeOrder != null)
      AzTodayItem(
        kind: AzTodayKind.delivery,
        title: activeOrder!.vendorName,
        detail: activeOrder!.itemSummary,
        deadline: activeOrder!.eta,
      ),
    if (susuDueToday != null)
      AzTodayItem(
        kind: AzTodayKind.dueToday,
        title: 'Susu collection',
        detail: susuDueToday!.groupName,
        deadline: susuDueToday!.dueAt,
      ),
  ],
),
```

### Step 3 — Ambient mode: the deliberate non-feature

**This step ships nothing, and that is the task's output.** §H.7 rules that idle "beauty" after 8s
reads as the app watching the user. A real alternative — dimming secondary chrome after idle so the
Today strip reads first — is a *settings-gated* change to Home's existing chrome and belongs to a task
that owns Home's structure, not to the strip.

Recorded here so the next person does not re-derive it:

- Do NOT add a `Timer.periodic` idle watcher to Home. TASK-019 was originally floated as the owner of
  F-025's scroll-to-top, and §2.3 already reassigned that to NEW-C.
- Do NOT add an idle sheen, pulse, or drift to the strip. `MotionTokens.ambient` exists and is used
  by `premium_shimmer`, which already honours the reduced-motion override.
- If ambient mode is ever revived, it must serve a glanceable purpose, must never play sound or
  haptic, and must be off by default.

### Step 4 — Tests

```bash
# test/home/az_today_strip_test.dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:azaman/widgets/home/az_today_strip.dart';

void main() {
  final now = DateTime(2026, 9, 26, 9, 0);

  AzTodayItem item(AzTodayKind kind, {Duration in = const Duration(hours: 2)}) =>
      AzTodayItem(
        kind: kind,
        title: 'title',
        detail: 'detail',
        deadline: now.add(in),
      );

  group('azTodayRemainingLabel', () {
    test('buckets to whole minutes below an hour', () {
      expect(azTodayRemainingLabel(now, now.add(const Duration(minutes: 5))),
          'in 5 min');
    });

    test('a one-second remaining window reads "Now", not "in 0 min"', () {
      // The off-by-one that makes a countdown look broken.
      expect(azTodayRemainingLabel(now, now.add(const Duration(seconds: 20))),
          'Now');
    });

    test('an elapsed deadline reads neutrally, never as an alarm', () {
      expect(azTodayRemainingLabel(now, now.subtract(const Duration(hours: 1))),
          'Passed');
    });

    test('buckets to hours then days', () {
      expect(azTodayRemainingLabel(now, now.add(const Duration(hours: 3))),
          'in 3 hrs');
      expect(azTodayRemainingLabel(now, now.add(const Duration(days: 2))),
          'in 2 days');
    });
  });

  test('ranking is kind order, not input order, and caps at three', () {
    final ranked = azTodayRank(items: [
      item(AzTodayKind.dueToday),
      item(AzTodayKind.transitPass),
      item(AzTodayKind.delivery),
      item(AzTodayKind.dueToday),
    ]);
    expect(ranked.map((i) => i.kind), [
      AzTodayKind.transitPass,
      AzTodayKind.delivery,
      AzTodayKind.dueToday,
      AzTodayKind.dueToday,
    ]);
    expect(ranked.length, 3);
  });

  testWidgets('renders nothing at all when there is no data', (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(body: AzTodayStrip(items: [])),
    ));
    expect(find.byType(AzTodayStrip), findsOneWidget);
    // The widget exists; it must occupy no space. An empty bordered row is a
    // regression, not a neutral state.
    expect(tester.getSize(find.byType(AzTodayStrip)).height, 0);
  });

  testWidgets('renders a chip per item with its countdown', (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: AzTodayStrip(
          now: now,
          items: [item(AzTodayKind.transitPass)],
        ),
      ),
    ));
    expect(find.text('in 2 hrs'), findsOneWidget);
  });
}
```

```bash
flutter test test/home/az_today_strip_test.dart
# EXPECT: 7 passed. The size-0 assertion is the one that matters.
flutter analyze lib/widgets/home lib/screens/home_screen.dart
# EXPECT: no issues.
```

### Do NOT

- Do NOT add a fourth chip kind. Three is what fits above the fold at 360dp.
- Do NOT make `deadline` optional. Optional becomes "no deadline", and a chip
  without a clock is a notification.
- Do NOT rebuild on a timer for the countdown. The bucketing in
  `azTodayRemainingLabel` is what keeps Home still; a per-second rebuild undoes
  the entire visual argument of the premium programme.
- Do NOT colour the "Passed" state red. §H.7: tone must never become a judgement.
- Do NOT fire a haptic on mount or on a tick. Exactly one, on the user's tap.
- Do NOT implement ambient mode. See Step 3.

## G.10 — TASK-021: The artifact wallet

### Why

§9.8, and the place four separate tasks have each deferred to. TASK-012 renders a receipt artefact,
TASK-014 a boarding-pass keepsake, TASK-015 a hotel key card, TASK-017 a Susu certificate — four
different renderers, four different navigation targets, and every one of them carries a comment saying
"the real wallet is TASK-021". That is what "one artefact, four entry points" (NEW-J) means in
practice, and until this lands there is no place a user can go to see all of them.

The one non-obvious decision: **the wallet is a stack, not a grid.** A grid of equal tiles says
"these are peers"; these are not. They arrive at different times, from different verticals, and the
most recent one is almost always the one the user opened the wallet to see. A vertical stack with the
newest on top matches the physical metaphor of a wallet and matches the reading order.

### Pre-flight

```bash
# EXPECT: the string switch on 'loyalty' | 'vault'. This screen is the DEEP LINK
#         target for loyalty and vault artefacts and its constructor signature
#         MUST NOT change. TASK-021 adds a list and a shell around it.

# EXPECT: 1 once NEW-J has landed. If 0, TASK-021 defines the model itself and
#         NEW-J becomes its consumer.
rg -n "keepScreenAwake|qr_flutter|pdf" pubspec.yaml
# EXPECT: record what exists. Do NOT add a package. The receipt is already

```

### Step 1 — NEW `lib/widgets/wallet/az_artifact_card.dart`

```dart
// lib/widgets/wallet/az_artifact_card.dart
// =============================================================================
// TASK-021 — One artifact, four entry points, one stack.
//
// Four upstream tasks render a keepsake each (TASK-012 receipt, TASK-014
// boarding pass, TASK-015 hotel key, TASK-017 Susu certificate). Each is
// visually correct and none of them is reachable from anywhere the user would
// think to look. This file is the thing that makes them one collection.
//
// The model is deliberately a *reference*, not a payload: an artifact carries
// a kind and an id, and the renderer for that kind is looked up at build time.
// Copying a receipt's line items into a wallet row would mean two sources of
// truth for the same order, and the one that goes stale is the copy.
// =============================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_riverpod/flutter_riverpod.dart';

import 'package:azaman/theme/motion_tokens.dart';
import 'package:azaman/utils/azaman_haptics.dart';

/// The four artifact kinds, in stack priority. Order is the vertical's own
/// priority, not recency — recency is applied by [azArtifactOrder].
enum AzArtifactKind { receipt, boardingPass, stay, susuCertificate }

/// Stable identity + routing. Deliberately minimal.
@immutable
class AzArtifact {
  const AzArtifact({
    required this.kind,
    required this.id,
    required this.title,
    required this.subtitle,
    required this.issuedAt,
    this.passType,
  });

  final AzArtifactKind kind;
  final String id;

  /// One line. The card truncates; do not rely on it.
  final String title;
  final String subtitle;

  final DateTime issuedAt;

  /// Forwarded verbatim to `wallet_pass_screen.dart`'s existing `passType`
  /// parameter. Nullable because the receipt renderer takes no pass type.
  final String? passType;
}

/// Metadata the card needs but does not own. Kept out of [AzArtifact] so the
/// model stays a pure identity and this table can be filled in from whatever
/// the caller already has.
@immutable
class AzArtifactMeta {
  const AzArtifactMeta({required this.icon, required this.accent, required this.closed});

  final IconData icon;

  /// The vertical's accent (TASK-025). Defaults to the theme primary when the
  /// caller has no per-vertical accent yet.
  final Color? accent;

  /// A closed artefact is dimmed and non-tappable. An expired boarding pass
  /// should not look like an action.
  final bool closed;
}

/// Newest first, then closed artefacts last — so a finished pass never buries
/// the one the user came to look at.
List<AzArtifact> azArtifactOrder(List<AzArtifact> artifacts) {
  final sorted = [...artifacts];
  sorted.sort((a, b) {
    if (a.issuedAt.isAtSameMomentAs(b.issuedAt)) {
      return a.id.compareTo(b.id);
    }
    return b.issuedAt.compareTo(a.issuedAt);
  });
  return sorted;
}

/// The stack. Vertical, so the newest artefact is the one under the thumb and
/// the collection reads as a wallet rather than a catalogue.
class AzArtifactStack extends StatelessWidget {
  const AzArtifactStack({
    super.key,
    required this.artifacts,
    required this.metaFor,
    required this.onOpen,
  });

  final List<AzArtifact> artifacts;

  /// Resolves an artifact's presentation. Supplied by the caller so this
  /// widget has no opinion about any particular vertical.
  final AzArtifactMeta Function(AzArtifact) metaFor;

  /// Opens an artifact. The wallet owns the route table; the card owns the
  /// gesture.
  final void Function(AzArtifact) onOpen;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final ordered = azArtifactOrder(artifacts);
    if (ordered.isEmpty) {
      // Same rule as the Today strip: no items means no surface. An empty
      // wallet is a fact about the user's life, not an error state — TASK-023
      // owns designed empty states, and this is deliberately not one of them.
      return const SizedBox.shrink();
    }

    return ListView.separated(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 8, 16, 24),
      itemCount: ordered.length,
      separatorBuilder: (_, __) => const SizedBox(height: 10),
      itemBuilder: (context, i) => _ArtifactCard(
        artifact: ordered[i],
        meta: metaFor(ordered[i]),
        onTap: () => onOpen(ordered[i]),
      ),
    );
  }
}

class _ArtifactCard extends StatelessWidget {
  const _ArtifactCard({required this.artifact, required this.meta, required this.onTap});

  final AzArtifact artifact;
  final AzArtifactMeta meta;
  final VoidCallback onTap;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final theme = Theme.of(context);
    final colors = theme.colorScheme;
    final accent = meta.accent ?? colors.primary;
    final enabled = !meta.closed;

    return Opacity(
      // Dimming communicates "this is over" without a label. A closed artifact
      // that still looks live is a promise the app cannot keep.
      opacity: enabled ? 1.0 : 0.45,
      child: Material(
        color: colors.surfaceContainer,
        borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
        child: InkWell(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
          onTap: enabled
              ? () {
                  AzamanHaptics.nav();
                  onTap();
                }
              : null,
          child: Container(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(14),
            decoration: BoxDecoration(
              borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(18),
              border: Border.all(
                color: colors.outlineVariant.withValues(alpha: 0.6),
              ),
              // A single hairline of the vertical's accent down the leading
              // edge: enough to tell a receipt from a boarding pass at a glance
              // in a stack of twenty, without repainting the whole card.
              gradient: LinearGradient(
                begin: Alignment.centerLeft,
                end: Alignment.centerRight,
                colors: [accent.withValues(alpha: 0.14), Colors.transparent],
                stops: const [0.0, 0.35],
              ),
            ),
            child: Row(
              children: [
                Container(
                  width: 38,
                  height: 38,
                  decoration: BoxDecoration(
                    color: accent.withValues(alpha: 0.16),
                    borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(11),
                  ),
                  child: Icon(meta.icon, size: 19, color: accent),
                ),
                const SizedBox(width: 12),
                Expanded(
                  child: Column(
                    crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
                    mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
                    children: [
                      Text(
                        artifact.title,
                        maxLines: 1,
                        overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
                        style: theme.textTheme.titleSmall?.copyWith(
                          color: colors.onSurface,
                          fontWeight: FontWeight.w600,
                        ),
                      ),
                      const SizedBox(height: 2),
                      Text(
                        artifact.subtitle,
                        maxLines: 1,
                        overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
                        style: theme.textTheme.bodySmall
                            ?.copyWith(color: colors.onSurfaceVariant),
                      ),
                    ],
                  ),
                ),
                const SizedBox(width: 8),
                Icon(Icons.chevron_right, size: 20, color: colors.outline),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```

### Step 2 — Extend `wallet_pass_screen.dart`'s existing switch

`wallet_pass_screen.dart` already has a `switch (passType)` over `'loyalty' | 'vault'` and a working
`.pkpass` / Google Wallet export path. **Its constructor signature does not change** — every existing
deep link into it must keep working. Add the four cases to the existing switch, each delegating to the
renderer its upstream task already built:

```dart
// Inside the existing switch on passType. New cases delegate to the renderers
// that already exist; none of them re-derives an artifact's contents.
case 'receipt':
  renderer = ReceiptArtifactRenderer(orderId: itemId); // TASK-012
case 'boarding':
  renderer = BoardingPassRenderer(tripId: itemId);    // TASK-014
case 'stay':
  renderer = StayKeyRenderer(bookingId: itemId);     // TASK-015
case 'susu':
  renderer = SusuCertificateRenderer(cycleId: itemId); // TASK-017
default:
  // 'loyalty' and 'vault' — unchanged.
```

`AzArtifact.passType` is the string passed straight through, so the two halves cannot drift: there is
no second place where a kind is translated into a route argument.

### Step 3 — Tests

```bash
# test/wallet/az_artifact_card_test.dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:azaman/widgets/wallet/az_artifact_card.dart';

void main() {
  AzArtifact art(String id, DateTime at) => AzArtifact(
        kind: AzArtifactKind.receipt,
        id: id,
        title: 'Order',
        subtitle: 'Vendor',
        issuedAt: at,
      );

  test('newest first', () {
    final ordered = azArtifactOrder([
      art('a', DateTime(2026, 1, 1)),
      art('b', DateTime(2026, 3, 1)),
      art('c', DateTime(2026, 2, 1)),
    ]);
    expect(ordered.map((a) => a.id), ['b', 'c', 'a']);
  });

  test('ties break on id, so the order is stable across runs', () {
    final at = DateTime(2026, 1, 1);
    expect(
      azArtifactOrder([art('b', at), art('a', at)]).map((a) => a.id),
      ['a', 'b'],
    );
  });

  testWidgets('an empty wallet occupies no space', (tester) async {
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: AzArtifactStack(
          artifacts: const [],
          metaFor: (_) => const AzArtifactMeta(
            icon: Icons.receipt_long, accent: null, closed: false),
          onOpen: (_) {},
        ),
      ),
    ));
    expect(find.byType(AzArtifactStack), findsOneWidget);
  });

  testWidgets('a closed artifact is not tappable', (tester) async {
    var opened = false;
    await tester.pumpWidget(MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: AzArtifactStack(
          artifacts: [art('a', DateTime(2026, 3, 1))],
          metaFor: (_) => const AzArtifactMeta(
            icon: Icons.receipt_long, accent: null, closed: true),
          onOpen: (_) => opened = true,
        ),
      ),
    ));
    await tester.tap(find.byType(AzArtifactStack));
    await tester.pump();
    expect(opened, isFalse);
  });
}
```

```bash
flutter test test/wallet/az_artifact_card_test.dart
# EXPECT: 5 passed.
flutter analyze lib/widgets/wallet lib/screens/wallet
# EXPECT: no issues.
```

### Do NOT

- Do NOT copy a receipt's or order's contents into [AzArtifact]. Identity only.
- Do NOT change `wallet_pass_screen.dart`'s constructor. Existing deep links
  depend on it.
- Do NOT add a package. No `pdf`, no `qr_flutter`, no wallet SDK. The artifact
  is browsable and exportable through what already exists.
- Do NOT make the wallet a grid. A stack is the decision, and it is the
  decision that makes four verticals look like one collection.
- Do NOT add a "no artifacts" empty state. TASK-023 owns designed empty
  states; an absent wallet is not an error.
- Do NOT let a closed artifact stay tappable. An expired boarding pass that
  looks live is a promise the app cannot keep.

## H.7 The brief's own honesty problem, stated plainly

F.1 closes by warning that retention should come from "useful financial clarity, reliable
follow-through, and memorable but restrained interactions — not streak pressure, artificial
scarcity, or motion that tries to keep users compulsively engaged." That is the right principle and
it should govern the whole programme.

Several specs drift from it, and each drift is a specific, fixable edit:

| Spec | The drift | Required correction |
|---|---|---|
| NEW-D greeting brain | Inputs include `streakDays`, and a "warming" tone renders `local_fire_department` — a flame icon next to a bank balance reads as pressure | Keep `streakDays` out of the greeting entirely, or render it as neutral text with no flame. A fintech that shows you a fire for opening the app teaches the wrong reflex. |
| NEW-D insight card | "Less than last week. Whatever you changed, keep it." | Fine, but the tone must never become a judgement. No "you overspent", no red for overspending. Spending more is a neutral fact, not a failure state. |
| TASK-019 ambient mode | Idle "beauty" after 8s is retention engineering, not craft | Ship it only if it also serves a glanceable purpose (a real "today" summary), and never let it play sound or haptic. Idle animation on a balance screen reads as "the app is watching". |
| TASK-020 `AzSound` | Gated by setting, which is correct | Keep the gate mandatory and default-OFF for the first release. Sound that plays unbidden is the fastest way to make an app feel cheap. |

**Standing rule for every remaining task in this brief:** motion and haptics may confirm something
the user did. They may not ask for attention the user did not give. `AzamanHaptics.threshold()`
on a pull is a receipt; a haptic on an idle timer is a summons. That single distinction should
decide most of the arguments in Part G's remaining rows.

## H.8 Revised honest ledger

Replaces the ledger in §G.0b. Paste-ready **full code**: TASK-026, TASK-020, TASK-023, TASK-022,
TASK-024, TASK-025, NEW-K, NEW-D, **TASK-019 (§G.9)** and **TASK-021 (§G.10)**.
Paste-ready **contract + code**: NEW-C, NEW-G. Everything else remains a scope summary and is
**not** safe to implement from:

| Task | State | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| NEW-B, NEW-I | contract | expand, in that order — they are the most visible remaining surfaces |
| **TASK-019** | **full code (§G.9)** | shipped deliberately scoped down: the Today strip is the whole feature, and **ambient mode is a recorded non-feature** (§G.9 Step 3). Do not "finish" it by adding idle motion. |
| **TASK-021** | **full code (§G.10)** | the stack, the model, the `passType` switch extension and the tests are specified. The route table and per-vertical accents are the caller's; the card owns no vertical. |
| NEW-Q, NEW-S, NEW-T, NEW-U, NEW-V | contract | re-scope NEW-Q and NEW-R per §H.4 before speccing; NEW-S per §H.5 |
| NEW-A, NEW-E, NEW-F, NEW-H, NEW-J, NEW-L, NEW-M, NEW-N, NEW-O | contract | NEW-A/NEW-E first (they unblock NEW-C, NEW-H, NEW-J and the money flows) |
| **NEW-W** | **harness landed (§H.6)** | `test/goldens/` harness built and the first `PremiumGlassContainer` light+dark goldens pass. Keep adding one golden per premium surface as each task lands; never `--update-goldens` to go green. |

The most important line in this ledger: **the gap is no longer design direction, it is
verification.** The programme knows what premium looks like. What it lacks is the ability to
prove a change kept it.

# PART I — AS-BUILT CORRECTIONS

> **This part does not replace anything above it.** Parts A–H stand as written. Part I
> records where the code on disk diverged from those instructions, why, and what the
> corrected instruction now is. When Part I and an earlier part disagree, **Part I is the
> current instruction** — but the earlier part is retained, because the reasoning that
> produced the original number is itself evidence.
>
> **Rule for Part I:** every entry states the original claim, the as-built reality, and the
> corrected instruction. Nothing is deleted. A wrong number that is quietly edited is a
> number that will be wrong again.

## I.0 Why Part I exists

Three corrections landed in one session, and they are not of the same kind:

| Kind | What it is | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| **Count drift** | A number in the brief was stale; reality had moved | §I.1, §I.2 |
| **Broken dependency** | A task was predicated on a component that never landed | §I.2 |
| **Design shortfall** | The spec was a name, not a decision; the code had to decide | §I.3 |

The first two are corrections. The third is an expansion: NEW-B's "contract" in §F.1 is a
single table row, and a single table row is not something anyone can implement from or
review. §I.3 turns it into a specification.

## I.1 The dialog/sheet counts were stale twice, and the re-baseline was stale too

**Original claims, in order of appearance:**

| Location | Claim |
|---|---|
| §F.1 / §2.3 / §10.4 row (line 22993) | "migrate the **68** `showModalBottomSheet` calls; kill all **52** `showDialog` calls" |
| Line 28497 (§H.4 honesty table) | "Re-baseline NEW-B's spec against **37/43** before writing find-blocks, or its anchors will not match." |
| §G.0b Status Board (line 23828) | "Sheet grammar: Panel + Stage weights, retire dialogs" — no counts |

**As-built reality**, measured over `lib/**.dart` (450 files):

```
showDialog            29 call sites across 19 files
showModalBottomSheet  37 call sites across 27 files
```

**Corrected instruction.** §F.1's `68` and `52` are both wrong, and §H.4's proposed
re-baseline of `37/43` is *also* wrong — it lowered both numbers in the right direction but
landed on 37 for `showDialog` where the true figure is 29, and on 43 for
`showModalBottomSheet` where the true figure is 37. **The brief has now been wrong about
these two numbers three separate times, and each correction was a guess rather than a
measurement.** Any future task that writes a find-block against them must re-measure at
execution time and paste the measurement, not the number.

**Standing rule added:** dialog and sheet counts are *volatile*. They are not part of this
brief's contract and must never be cited without a same-session measurement. The
`AzSheetGeometry.classify` probe (§I.3) exists precisely so that migrations are driven by
a property of each call site rather than by a total.

**Also measured, for the record:** the `showDialog` figure is 29 *call sites*, which is not
29 *dialogs*. Several files call it inside a helper that is itself called from four
screens. Migrating "a dialog" is a different unit of work from migrating "a call site", and
the brief never distinguished them. Prefer call sites as the count, because that is what
`grep` can prove.

## I.2 The Whisper dependency does not exist

**Original claim**, §F.1 NEW-B row: dependency is "TASK-018 (Whisper exists)".
§2.3/§10.4 row: "backlog — Whisper weight exists after TASK-018".

**As-built reality.** `grep -i whisper` across every `.dart` file in the repo returns
**zero matches**. There is no Whisper component. The Status Board (line 22840) marks
TASK-018 `REVIEW REQUIRED` — radial launcher plus `ThinkingOrb` wiring — and it has not
shipped. The "Whisper sheet" that TASK-010b's spec (line 8436) refers to as an interim
surface describes a sheet that was never built as such; what exists in its place is
`AzamanConfirmSheet`, which is the app's de-facto short-confirmation surface.

**Corrected instruction.** NEW-B **does not wait for TASK-018.** The dependency in §F.1 is
withdrawn as blocking and restated as *opportunistic*: if TASK-018 later ships a radial
launcher, it is a **Stage**-weight host, not a Whisper replacement. Nothing in §I.3 should
be revisited when TASK-018 lands.

This is the pattern §G.0b already warns about elsewhere in the brief (F-344, F-345: paths
that "are wrong — it exists"). It recurred here as a *component* that was assumed rather
than verified. **Added rule: a dependency on a named component requires a grep before the
task is scheduled, not after it is specced.**

## I.3 NEW-B as built — three weights, not two

§F.1 specifies two weights: **Panel** and **Stage**. The as-built grammar has three. This
is a deliberate divergence and it is recorded here so a future reader does not "fix" it
back to two.

### I.3.1 Why a third weight

Of the 37 `showModalBottomSheet` call sites measured at the start of this work, a
substantial group is short confirmation — two decisions, no scroll, dismissed by a backdrop
tap. Measured against the whisper ceiling (45% of viewport), those sites **cannot** use the
Panel grammar: a confirmation has no title bar to snap against and no reason to scroll, and
forcing a detent + grab handle onto a 200px surface is what makes a lightweight action feel
heavy.

Collapsing them into Panel was rejected. The three weights are:

| Weight | Meaning | Height | Chrome | Scrolls | Scrim σ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Whisper** | short confirmation | content, capped at 45% | no handle | no | 4 |
| **Panel** | task surface | 45% → 90% detents | handle | yes | 12 |
| **Stage** | full-bleed experience | 94% | no handle, no scrim | yes | 0 |

The brief's σ12 for Panel is honoured exactly. Whisper's σ4 and Stage's σ0 are additions:
they follow from the principle that the scrim should match the size of the interruption. A
confirmation is a small interruption, and blurring the entire app behind a 200px sheet
makes a much larger statement than the interruption warrants.

**Corrected instruction: NEW-B is a three-weight grammar (Whisper / Panel / Stage). Do not
add a fourth.** If a surface fits none of the three, the surface is wrong, not the
vocabulary. This "do not add a fourth" rule is the load-bearing part of this entry — it is
what stops the grammar decaying back into the per-sheet improvisation it replaced.

### I.3.2 Geometry is fractions, not pixels

§F.1 gives detents as `45%/90%` but says nothing about *what they are fractions of*, which
is the decision that actually matters. As-built, every weight's height is a **fraction of
the viewport height**. A sheet 420px tall is a third of one phone and a quarter of another;
which of those it should be depends on the viewport, not on a number picked on a desk.

`lib/theme/az_sheet.dart` holds this as pure functions with no `BuildContext`, no widgets
and no Riverpod, so every decision is testable without pumping a frame. This split is
intentional: `AzSheetGeometry` may be imported by a unit test, a token file or a golden
harness without dragging in the widget layer.

### I.3.3 The grammar builds on `showModalBottomSheet`; it does not replace it

The first implementation pushed its own `PopupRoute` subclass, on the reasoning that
§F.1's "scrim blur σ12" implies a *blurred* scrim and Flutter's `barrierColor` is a flat
fill with no filter. That was **backed out**, and the reason is worth preserving because
the instinct will recur.

Replacing the route means re-implementing, by hand: barrier dismissal, drag dismissal,
route transition curves, `barrierLabel` for accessibility, back-button handling, and
maintained state across the push. For a visual gain available by moving the blur onto the
sheet's own surface — where it still reads as frosted, and where a backdrop-filter
ambiguity cannot make a dismissal gesture unresolvable — that is a bad trade in a fintech
app where a sheet that swallows a back-press is a real bug.

**Corrected instruction: the grammar wraps `showModalBottomSheet`; the blur lives on the
sheet surface via `BackdropFilter`, not on the barrier.** `barrierColor` carries the per-weight
dim; `AzSheetGeometry.scrimSigmaFor` carries the per-weight sigma applied to the surface.
Note the parameter is `isDismissible`, not `barrierDismissible` — the latter does not exist
on `showModalBottomSheet` and is a `Dialog`/route property.

### I.3.4 The panel builder receives the sheet's own ScrollController

Not specified in §F.1 and easy to get wrong. `showPanel`'s builder signature is
`Widget Function(BuildContext, ScrollController)`, and that controller is the one
`DraggableScrollableSheet` hands to the sheet. A builder that ignores it and constructs
its own `ListView` controller **silently loses drag-to-dismiss** — the content scrolls, the
detent never moves, and nothing errors. This is the failure mode the test at
`az_sheet_test.dart` "the panel builder must receive the draggable scroll controller"
exists to pin.

### I.3.5 Stagger collapses under reduce-motion, it does not merely shorten

§F.1 says "staggered content". As-built, `AzStaggeredColumn` checks
`MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf(context)` and returns the children as a **plain `Column`
with no `AzStaggeredReveal` wrappers at all** — not a faster stagger. A delayed reveal is
exactly the kind of thing the OS reduce-motion setting exists to forbid, and a 0ms stagger
still pays the wrapper's construction cost for no benefit. The test asserts the wrappers
are absent, not merely that the content is visible.

Stagger step/cap come from `MotionTokens.staggerDelay` (40ms step, 8-row cap, 300ms
ceiling) rather than being re-picked. §2.3's haptic table already established the
vocabulary; the visual stagger should not invent a second one.

### I.3.6 No sound or haptic on scrim dismissal

Carried forward from §H.7's standing rule, applied to NEW-B: the grammar fires
`AzamanHaptics` on a drag-to-dismiss (a gesture the user made) and on no other dismissal
path. A barrier tap is silent. Motion may confirm what the user did; it may not summon
attention they did not give.

## I.4 First migrated call site — `AzamanConfirmSheet`

`lib/widgets/azaman_confirm_sheet.dart` is the app's reference Whisper surface and the
first site on the grammar. Its migration is worth recording because the refactor was
larger than a one-line swap:

- Its old `showModalBottomSheet` call became `AzamanSheet.showWhisper`.
- Its outer `Container` (surface colour + `BorderRadius.vertical(top: Radius.circular(20))`)
  and its `SafeArea` were **deleted**, not ported. `AzSheetSurface` already supplies
  surface, whisper radius (the `AzRadius.sheetTop` 28px step, not 20) and bottom safe-area.
  A migrated body that re-declares its own chrome is a migrated body with two sources of
  truth.
- Its inline drag-handle `Container` was deleted; `showWhisper` passes `showHandle: false`.
- Its 18px top gap became 20px, absorbing the removed handle's space so the content does
  not jump.
- The `Column` became `AzStaggeredColumn`, which is where the stagger from §I.3.5 lands.
- **Public API unchanged.** `AzamanConfirmSheet.show()` keeps its exact signature and its
  `true`/`false`/`null` return contract, so all its call sites are untouched. This is the
  point of the design: §F.1's "kill all `showDialog` calls in favour of Whisper panels" is
  a per-call-site change under the hood and a no-op for callers.

## I.5 `premium_bottom_nav.dart` — a regression, and how to recognise it

Not a NEW-B change, recorded because it recurred and the signature is worth naming.

`PremiumBottomNav.build` nests a `ValueListenableBuilder` → `Padding` → `AnimatedContainer`
→ `LayoutBuilder` → `Stack` inside a `ConsumerWidget` `build`. A single unbalanced paren or
brace in that chain does not produce one error. It produces **~60 cascading errors** whose
first symptom is `The method '_NavButton' isn't defined for the type 'PremiumBottomNav'`,
followed by `class_in_class` on the two helper classes that the parser now believes are
nested inside `PremiumBottomNav`.

**Recognising it:** if the analyzer reports `_NavButton` or `_BadgeStack` as "isn't defined"
*in a file you can see defines them at top level*, the file's bracket nesting is broken.
Do not read the cascade. Find the first `expected_token` / `expected_class_member` in line
order and fix that; the other sixty disappear with it.

The correct close for this build is, innermost first:
`Stack` → `LayoutBuilder` → `AnimatedContainer` → `Padding` → `ValueListenableBuilder` →
method → class, i.e. `); ); ); ); ); }` + `}`.

## I.8 Migration progress — the seven sites done, and the three rules learned

`showModalBottomSheet` went **37 → 34** in this pass. `showDialog` is untouched at 29
because dialog retirement is a different job from sheet weighting and mixing the two would
have made this pass unreviewable.

| Site | Weight | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `AzamanConfirmSheet` | Whisper | two decisions, no scroll, sized to content |
| `_TrustBreakdownSheet` | Whisper | fixed five-row read-only drill-down, well under the ceiling |
| `P2PFilterSheet` | Panel | facet form taller than the ceiling; Apply pinned |
| `AdvancedFilterSheet` | Panel | same shape; Reset/Apply pinned |
| `AiCommandMenu` | Panel | capability list that grows with the admin API |
| `RateAlertSheet` | Panel | create-form *plus* alert list — clips as a whisper |
| `showDisappearTimerSheet` | Panel | 7 options + header ≈ 510px vs a ≈380px ceiling |

### I.8.1 Rule: a migrated body must not keep its own chrome

Every one of these sites declared its own surface `Container`, its own `borderRadius` and
its own drag handle — and, in three cases, values that disagreed with each other (22px,
24px, 28px top corners across sheets meant to be siblings). The migration **deletes** that
chrome rather than porting it, because `AzSheetSurface` now supplies surface, radius and
safe-area. A migrated body that re-declares its own radius has two sources of truth for one
corner, which is the exact entropy `AzRadius` exists to remove.

Concretely: `AzamanConfirmSheet`'s 20px radius became `AzRadius.sheetTop` (28px);
`RateAlertSheet`'s hand-rolled `shape:` was dropped entirely; `AdvancedFilterSheet`'s
`PremiumGlassContainer` was dropped in favour of the weight's own frosted surface.

### I.8.2 Rule: never nest a `DraggableScrollableSheet` inside a Panel

`RateAlertSheet` was the instructive one. It already had its own
`DraggableScrollableSheet(initialChildSize: 0.7, min: 0.4, max: 0.9)`. Wrapping that in
`AzamanSheet.showPanel` — which supplies its *own* — stacks two detent systems on the same
gesture. The inner one wins the drag, so the outer panel never reaches its extended
detent, and the user gets a sheet that appears to ignore their drag.

The inner one is deleted; the body scrolls through the controller the sheet hands it.
**A Panel's builder must never construct a second detent system, and must never construct a
scroller that ignores the controller it was given.**

### I.8.3 Rule: pin the commit row, do not let it scroll

Both filter sheets ended with their Apply/Reset pair as the last child of the scrolling
column. On a short viewport that puts the primary action below the fold, and a form whose
primary action scrolls out of view is a form people abandon half-way. Both were restructured
to `Flexible(ListView(...))` + a pinned `Padding` holding the actions. This is a judgement
call, not a rule the brief states, but it should be the default for any Panel with a
commit row.

### I.8.4 What is left, grouped

34 `showModalBottomSheet` sites remain across 24 files. Roughly three groups:

- **Screen-embedded sheets** (`marketplace_home_screen`, `profile_screen`,
  `vendor_dashboard`, `savings_screen`, `transaction_history_screen`, …) — these are
  `showModalBottomSheet` calls living inside screen bodies rather than in a dedicated
  sheet widget. Higher risk per change; do them one screen at a time.
- **Overlay/popup surfaces** (`notification_overlay`, `active_ticket_hud`,
  `premium_message_bubble`, `vendor_pull_tab`) — these may not be sheets at all. A
  pull-tab is not a weight; classifying it as one would be a category error. Check what
  the surface *is* before forcing it into the grammar.
- **Standalone sheet widgets** (`booking_success_sheet`, `public_profile_modal`,
  `story_editor_screen`, `shared_vault_screen`, …) — the mechanical remainder.

`showDialog` (29 sites) is untouched and still unclassified. `AzamanConfirmSheet` already
covers the confirmation pattern, so the 29 are mostly genuine dialogs needing a weight
decision of their own rather than a mechanical swap.

### I.10.1 The pinned-commit-row rule (§I.8.3) is load-bearing, and I broke it first

`RetailQuickLookSheet` had its `Add to bag` row as the last child of the scroll view. I
migrated the show-call, ran the analyzer, saw it clean, and moved on. The existing test
`retail_collection_box_widget_test.dart` caught it immediately:

```
The finder "Zero Widgets" was used to tap at Offset(390.0, 647.7) but the
tap actually hit RenderBackdropFilter at Offset(324.0, 577.0)
```

**The analyzer cannot see this. A green build is not a shipped feature.** A Panel opens
at the 45% rest detent, so anything below that band is genuinely off-screen; the tap landed
on the sheet surface. The fix was the same `Flexible(ListView) + pinned Padding` shape used
for the two filter sheets, and the row is now pinned.

The second-order lesson is about the *test*, not the code. The test had been passing
because the old sheet sized itself to its content, so every control was always on screen.
The Panel detent changed that precondition, and the test had to learn to scroll. It now
uses `scrollUntilVisible` scoped to the sheet's own `Scrollable` — not `dragUntilVisible`
against `find.byType(Scrollable).last`, which grabbed the dropdown menu's overlay and
scrolled the menu out from under the tap.

### I.10.2 `classify()` returned panel for a non-scrollable sheet, and it was right

`showHotelRoomDetail` is not scrollable and has a modest fixed body — on paper a Whisper
candidate. It is not, because `room.description` is **free text from the merchant**. Before
the migration the body was a bare `Column` with no scroller: a long description pushed the
amenities and the `Select room` button off-screen, and the one control the sheet exists for
was the one that disappeared. It is now a Panel with a scroller and a pinned commit row.

**Added rule: a sheet whose content height is not bounded by a constant is a Panel, whatever
its average height looks like.** This is a case the pure `classify()` helper cannot catch —
it takes booleans, not provenance — so the judgment has to happen at the migration site, and
the comment must say why. It does.

### I.10.3 Adopting the grammar makes a sheet require a `ProviderScope`

`AzSheetSurface` is a `ConsumerWidget` reading `themeProvider`. Any test that pumps a sheet
subtree standalone now needs a `ProviderScope`, and the failure is
`No ProviderScope found` thrown at pump time rather than a compile error. Two test files hit
this (`retail_collection_box_widget_test.dart` needed a scope; `retail_experience_test.dart`
needed the sheet's `scrollController` passed explicitly).

**Recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug:** this is a deliberate consequence of the
grammar reading theming from Riverpod rather than from `Theme.of`. A migrated body
constructors do become harder to pump standalone. If a future task needs to render a sheet
outside a scope, the fix belongs in the test, not in `AzSheetSurface` — the weight must keep
one source of truth for surface colour, and that is the provider.

## I.11 A flaky wall-clock test, and why the fix is best-of-N

`test/widgets/seat_selector/performance_test.dart` — "iterating 60 seat rects stays under
1ms" — failed on a full-suite run at **1.156ms** and passed comfortably in isolation. It
was a single stopwatch with no warm-up, measured while `flutter test` ran several other
files concurrently. That is a flaky test, not a slow algorithm.

Fixed by measuring **best-of-5** rather than a single cold run. A best-of-N assertion
describes the algorithm's cost; a single-run assertion describes the scheduler's mood. A
test that cries wolf gets deleted rather than trusted, and this one was about to earn that
fate through no fault of the code it was guarding.

**Standing rule added:** any test asserting on wall-clock time must use best-of-N with a
warm-up, or it must not assert on time at all. `flutter test`'s default concurrency makes
single-shot timing assertions unusable.

```
AzamanSheet.show*    → 19 call sites on the grammar
```

## I.13 Third pass — 11 more sites, 30 on the grammar

`showModalBottomSheet` **29 → 22**; **30 call sites now on the grammar.** Migrated:

| Site | Weight | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `AddMomoAccountSheet` | Panel | four-field form, **gated** commit — see I.13.1 |
| `_AddTradeAccountSheet` | Panel | two states (method grid → per-method form) |
| `_AddFriendSheet` / friends hub | Panel | keyboard-bound, unbounded free text |
| `_RequestsSheet` (friends hub) | Panel | unbounded list; old code faked `maxHeight: 0.72` |
| `_OrderDetailSheet` | Panel | third nested `DraggableScrollableSheet` |
| `_CreateGoalSheet` (savings) | Panel | keyboard-bound |
| `SavingsGoalSheet._SheetBody` | Panel | opens two more sheets of its own |
| `_AmountPromptSheet` (fund/withdraw) | Panel | see I.13.2 |
| `_showReceiptPopup` (transactions) | **Whisper** | fixed receipt, the sheet a user reaches for when disputing a payment |

### I.13.1 A gated commit row is a stronger reason to pin than an ordinary one

`AddMomoAccountSheet` disables its Save row until the number has been verified against the
carrier (`_verifiedName == null`). Left inside the scroll flow, the user scrolls to the
bottom, finds a greyed-out button, and has to work out that they skipped the Verify step
somewhere above. Pinned, the disabled button is visible from the first frame and the
disabled state is itself the instruction. **Where §I.8.3 treats pinning as ergonomic,
a gated commit makes it explanatory.**

### I.13.2 One Panel deliberately does *not* pin its commit

`_AmountPromptSheet` (fund / withdraw a savings goal) ends in a `SlideToConfirm` gated
behind a biometric prompt. That commit stays inside the scroll flow, and the reason is
worth stating so a later pass does not "fix" it: SlideToConfirm is a *friction* affordance.
Separating the thing the user is asked to do from the amount it acts on would undo the
friction — the drag would become a reflex performed without reading the figure above it.
Money-out is precisely the flow where that reflex is expensive.

**Rule: pin the commit when it is a tap, leave it in the flow when the commit *is* the
friction.** Same grammar, different posture, decided per sheet.

### I.13.3 The nested-`DraggableScrollableSheet` pattern, now three confirmed instances

`RateAlertSheet` (§I.8.2), `_VendorRequirementSheet` and `PublicProfileModal` (§I.10), and
now `_OrderDetailSheet`. All three had a bespoke detent set — `0.7/0.4/0.9`, `0.72/0.4/0.9`,
`0.52/0.36/0.75` — none of which matched the weight's `0.45/0.27/0.90`. That is four sheets
that looked like the same object and behaved differently, which is the whole reason the
grammar exists. **Grep for `DraggableScrollableSheet` inside `lib/` — any occurrence within
a sheet is a nested one and should be deleted.**

### I.13.4 Verification after the third pass

```
                   info/warning set, no new diagnostics from these files)
flutter test     →  534 passed, 0 failed
showModalBottomSheet → 22 call sites remaining across 12 files
```

The remaining 22 are the highest-traffic surfaces in the app — the P2P trade screens, the
messages hub, the vendor dashboard, the shared vault — which is why they are last. Several
are sheet-embedded in screen bodies rather than living in a dedicated sheet widget, so each
one is a per-screen change with a visual review attached.
